definition_zh: 加班；加班费；加时赛；超时的
definition_en: time worked beyond one's regular working hours, or a period of extra play added when a game is tied
core_image: 下班铃响过之后，灯还亮着，时间被往后多拨了一段
scene: 项目截止日期快到了，同事们下班后仍在加班。 The whole team worked overtime to finish the project before the deadline.
sceneCN: 这里 overtime 是「加班；超时工作」（第 1 个义项：超出正常工作的时间）；句意：为了在截止日期前完成项目，全队都在加班。

pos.zh: 加班时间；加班费；加时赛

derivatives.zh: over（过度）+ work（工作），义为「过度劳累；使工作过量」，侧重过量而非超时
基础词 over 本身，义为「在……之上；超过」，是构词的来源成分
part（部分）+ time（时间），义为「兼职的」，与 overtime 的「全职额外时间」形成对照
full（全部）+ time（时间），义为「全职的」，指正常工作时段
time（时间）+ -ly 后缀，义为「及时的」，与 overtime 共享 time 词根

senses.title: Time worked beyond regular hours
senses.definition: time spent working in addition to one's normal working hours
senses.definitionCN: 在正常工作时间之外继续工作的时间
senses.example: The staff were angry because they had to work overtime every week.
senses.exampleCN: 员工们很生气，因为他们每周都得加班。
senses.why: The core image is time pushed beyond a boundary; the working day has an edge, and overtime is what spills over it.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是时间越过边界：工作日有一条「界线」，overtime 就是漫出这条界线的那部分时间。

senses.title: Extra pay for extra hours
senses.definition: payment, usually at a higher rate, made for hours worked beyond the regular schedule
senses.definitionCN: 对超出正常工时的工作所支付的报酬，通常按更高费率计算
senses.example: She earns double overtime on public holidays.
senses.exampleCN: 她在法定节假日能拿到双倍加班费。
senses.why: Because the extra time costs the worker more, the word naturally extends to the money that compensates that time.
senses.whyCN: 多出的时间意味着更大的付出，于是这个词自然延伸到「补偿这段时间的钱」，即加班费。

senses.title: Extra playing time in a tied game
senses.definition: an additional period of play added when a sports game ends in a tie, to decide the winner
senses.definitionCN: 体育比赛打成平局后追加的比赛时段，用于决出胜负
senses.example: The game went into overtime after a scoreless second half.
senses.exampleCN: 下半场双方均未进球，比赛进入加时赛。
senses.why: A tied game has used up its allotted time but lacks a result, so more time must be granted — the same 'time beyond the limit' image.
senses.whyCN: 平局意味着规定时间用完却仍无结果，只能再「拨」一段时间——依旧是「超出限定的时间」这一核心意象。

senses.title: Beyond the usual or expected time
senses.definition: lasting or continuing longer than the time that was planned or agreed
senses.definitionCN: 持续的时间超过原定或约定的时间
senses.example: The negotiations ran overtime and finished near midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判超时了，快到午夜才结束。
senses.why: Once a schedule sets a limit, any excess is measured against it; overtime names whatever runs past the mark.
senses.whyCN: 日程一旦划定了限线，超出的部分就要以它为参照来衡量；overtime 指的就是越过刻度的那段时间。

senses.title: Working or done beyond regular hours
senses.definition: relating to or taking place during hours worked beyond the normal schedule
senses.definitionCN: 与超出正常工时的工作相关的；发生在加班时间里的
senses.example: He claimed overtime pay for the overtime hours he logged.
senses.exampleCN: 他为自己记录的加班时间申请了加班费。
senses.why: The noun hardens into an adjective when the phrase is used to label things — hours, pay, rules — connected with extra time.
senses.whyCN: 当名词被用来给「工时、报酬、规定」等事物贴标签时，就固化成了形容词，表示「属于加班时段的」。

senses.title: To work beyond regular hours
senses.definition: to work more hours than the regular schedule requires
senses.definitionCN: 工作的时间超出正常排班的要求
senses.example: The warehouse overtimes during the holiday rush every year.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢节假日旺季，仓库都要加班。
senses.why: English freely turns compounds like this into verbs; the action of spending extra time becomes the activity itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语习惯把这类复合词转成动词，「花费额外时间」这一状态被直接当作动作来说。

senses.title: Excess or surplus time in general
senses.definition: any amount of time that exceeds what was allotted or expected
senses.definitionCN: 任何超出原有分配或预期的额外时间
senses.example: The recording captured ten minutes of overtime beyond the planned interview.
senses.exampleCN: 录音比计划采访时多录了十分钟的超时内容。
senses.why: Stripped of work and sport, the word keeps its bare arithmetic: allotted time plus whatever spills over.
senses.whyCN: 去掉工作和比赛的语境，这个词保留了最朴素的算术含义：规定时间，加上漫出来的那部分。

senses.title: Long beyond what is reasonable
senses.definition: used to stress that something continues for far longer than is sensible or healthy
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调某事持续得远超合理或健康的限度
senses.example: Working overtime night after night, she slowly wore herself down.
senses.exampleCN: 夜复一夜地超时工作，她慢慢把自己拖垮了。
senses.why: The prefix over- already hints at 'too much'; repeated or extreme overtime shades from neutral description into warning.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 over- 本身带「过度」的暗示；反复或极端的超时让这个词从中性描述滑向警示意味。

intro.en: Overtime is a transparent English compound of over and time, built within English rather than borrowed.
intro.cn: overtime 是由 over 与 time 直接复合成的英语本族词，并非外来借词。

items.en: The reconstructed root *uper, meaning 'over, above', underlies over; a separate root *deh₂- 'to divide' is traditionally linked with time through the notion of divided periods.
items.cn: 重构词根 *uper（意为「在上、越过」）是 over 的来源；time 则一般认为可追溯到 *deh₂-「切分」，与「划分出的时段」概念相关（此联系属传统推测）。

items.en: Old English had ofer 'over, above' and tīma 'limited space of time, season'; both were core everyday words.
items.cn: 古英语已有 ofer（在上、越过）与 tīma（有限的时间段、时节），两者都是日常核心词。

items.en: The compound idea of 'time beyond' appears in phrases before the fused form; over + time combinations surface in late Middle English contexts of exceeding set periods.
items.cn: 「超出之时」的概念先以短语形式出现，over 与 time 的复合形式在晚期中古英语「超出约定期限」的语境中露头。

items.en: By the 17th century overtime is recorded for time exceeding an allowance or deadline; the industrial workplace later fixed its labour sense, and 19th-century sport added the tie-breaker sense.
items.cn: 17 世纪起 overtime 已用于指超出配额或期限的时间；后来工业化职场固定了其劳动含义，19 世纪体育又衍生出平局决胜的加时义。

items.en: Today overtime covers extra work hours, the pay for them, extra sports periods, and adjectival or adverbial uses, all from one image: time past the limit.
items.cn: 如今 overtime 兼指加班时间、加班费、体育加时，并可用作形容词和副词，全部源自同一意象：越过限度的时间。

note.en: Overtime looks simple, but it sits inside a busy family of over- compounds and time words that learners often mix up.
note.cn: overtime 看似简单，却身处 over- 复合词与 time 词族的密集地带，学习者容易混淆。

entries.definition: to work too much, or excessive work
entries.definitionCN: 过度工作；劳累过度——与 overtime 同用 over- 前缀，但侧重「量过多」而非「时超限」

entries.definition: above one's head, or regular business costs not tied to output
entries.definitionCN: 头顶上方的；（企业）日常经费、管理费用——只与 overtime 拼写相近、同含 over-，词义完全不同

entries.definition: an unintentional failure to notice, or the supervision of work
entries.definitionCN: 疏忽；监管——形近词，共享 over- 前缀但语义走向不同

entries.definition: hours worked in addition to the normal schedule
entries.definitionCN: 额外的工时——与 overtime 第 1 义几乎等义的口语说法

entries.definition: additional time, especially added to a tied football match (British usage)
entries.definitionCN: 加时（英式足球常用说法）——与美式 overtime 的加时赛义对应

entries.definition: working fewer hours than a full schedule
entries.definitionCN: 兼职的、非全日的——与 overtime 的「超出全职工时」形成反向对照

normalIntro.en: Break the word into its two honest parts and the meanings fall into place.
normalIntro.cn: 把这个词拆成老实的两半，各种义项便各归其位。

normal.en: over + time = time that goes over the limit.
normal.cn: over（越过）+ time（时间）＝越过限度的那段时间。

normal.en: The factory whistle blows, but the clock keeps running — that extra run is overtime.
normal.cn: 下班哨声已响，钟却还在走——多走的那段就是「加班」。

normal.en: Overtime pay: the extra time was sold, so the extra time is bought back at a higher price.
normal.cn: 加班费：多卖的时间，自然要按更高的价买回来。

normal.en: Score tied, clock at zero, referee adds five more minutes: overtime in sport.
normal.cn: 比分持平、时钟归零、裁判再补五分钟：这就是体育里的「加时赛」。

normal.en: Family: overwork (too much work), overhead (above the head / fixed costs), overtime (beyond the time limit).
normal.cn: 词族：overwork（工作过量）、overhead（头顶／管理费用）、overtime（超过时限）。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of water filled to the line, then one more drop makes it spill — the spilled minutes are overtime.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯水已到刻度线，再多一滴就溢出——溢出的那几分钟就是「超时」。

abstract.en: Imagine a rubber band of time stretched past its marking: taut, extra, costing more.
abstract.cn: 想象时间的橡皮筋被拉过刻度：绷紧、超额、代价更高。

abstract.en: See the office lights still on after everyone leaves — one lamp glowing late is overtime made visible.
abstract.cn: 看见人走光后办公室仍亮着的灯——深夜独亮的一盏灯就是「加班」的具象。

examples.en: The engineers worked overtime for three weeks to launch the product on schedule.
examples.cn: 工程师们连续加班三周，好让产品如期上线。

examples.en: Workers who put in overtime are legally entitled to overtime pay.
examples.cn: 加班的员工依法有权获得加班费。

examples.en: The final went into overtime, and the crowd refused to leave their seats.
examples.cn: 决赛进入加时赛，观众们不肯离开座位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧瓦·太姆」——「哦哇，太‘叹’了！」下班点早过了还要干，员工一声哀叹：又要加班了，时间真是‘太’漫出‘界’了。

root: overtime 是英语本族复合词：over（古英语 ofer，源自原始印欧语重构词根 *uper「在上、越过」）+ time（古英语 tīma「有限时段」，一般认为与原始印欧语 *deh₂-「切分」相关，此联系属传统推测）。字面义即「越过限度的时间」，加班、加班费、加时赛等义项均由此长出。

sensesIntro.en: From the bare image of time past a limit, the word grows into work hours, extra pay, sports extra periods, and beyond.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「越过限度的时间」这一朴素意象出发，词义依次长出加班工时、加班报酬、体育加时以及引申的「过久」等义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: time spilling over a fixed boundary
core.cn: 核心意象：时间漫过一条固定界线

branches.en: A schedule sets the boundary, and the hours worked past it are overtime.
branches.cn: 日程划出界线，界线之外继续工作的时数就是「加班」（义项 01）。

branches.en: The spilled hours are compensated at a higher rate: overtime pay.
branches.cn: 漫出的时间按更高费率补偿，即「加班费」（义项 02）。

branches.en: A tied game needs more minutes to find a winner: overtime in sport.
branches.cn: 平局的比赛需要再补时间决胜负，即体育「加时赛」（义项 03）。

branches.en: Any excess beyond what was allotted, in talks or recordings, is overtime.
branches.cn: 谈判、录音等场合超出原定安排的部分也是「超时／多余时间」（义项 04 · 07）。

branches.en: As adjective, verb, or warning, overtime names work beyond limits and the toll of too much of it.
branches.cn: 作形容词、动词或带警示意味时，overtime 指「超时的工作」及其「过久」的代价（义项 05 · 06 · 08）。

intro.en: Overtime is built from a native prefix-like adverb and a native noun; the same parts spawn a large compound family.
intro.cn: overtime 由本族的副词性成分与本族名词复合而成，同样的构件派生出一个庞大的复合词家族。

latinIntro.en: Although the compound itself is Germanic, the underlying parts connect to Latin kin through the shared Indo-European heritage.
latinIntro.cn: 复合词本身虽属日耳曼系统，但其底层成分通过印欧共同遗产与拉丁语同族词遥相呼应。

items.example: overflow — the river overflows after the storm
items.exampleCN: overflow（溢出）——暴雨过后河水漫过堤岸

items.meaning: a period or the continuum of duration
items.example: timetable — check the timetable before boarding
items.exampleCN: timetable（时刻表）——上车前先查时刻表

items.example: They logged three hours of overtime
items.exampleCN: 他们登记了三小时加班时间

items.example: Doctors warned him not to overwork
items.exampleCN: 医生告诫他不要操劳过度

items.example: I overslept and missed the bus
The new brand overtook its rival in sales
items.exampleCN: 新品牌销量赶超了对手

items.meaning: fail to notice, or have a view over
items.example: She overlooked one detail in the report
items.exampleCN: 她忽略了报告里的一个细节

items.example: He spent a lifetime studying ants
The shop opens in the daytime only

definition_zh: 短语；词组；措辞；说法；乐句；用言语表达
definition_en: a small group of words that works as a unit, the particular way something is worded, a short passage in music, or to express something in words
core_image: 几块写着一个词的小木牌被细线串成一串，挂在说话人的嘴前
scene: 老师在黑板上写下一句话，用粉笔把其中三个词圈在一起，说这一小串不能拆开单独理解。 She underlined the phrase twice before moving to the next line.
sceneCN: 这里 phrase 指「短语、词组」（第 1 个义项：几个词固定组合成一个单位）；句意为她把那个短语画了两遍才看下一行。图中可辨识物件：黑板、粉笔圈、串成一串的小木牌。

derivatives.zh: 由 phrase 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「短语的；由短语构成的」
由 phrase 加 -ing 构成，义为「措辞方式；乐句的处理」
由希腊语词干 phras- 加 -ology 构成，义为「措辞法；用语」
由前缀 para-（在旁边）加 phrase 构成，义为「换一种说法；改述」

senses.title: A small group of words forming a unit
senses.definition: a short group of words that acts as a single unit inside a sentence, such as a noun phrase or a verb phrase
senses.definitionCN: 在句子内部作为一个整体起作用的一小组词，如名词短语或动词短语
senses.example: The phrase in brackets can be left out.
senses.exampleCN: 括号里的那个短语可以省略。
senses.why: Greek phrasis named a manner of speaking, and this sense keeps that shape: a handful of words held together as one block of speech rather than counted one by one.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 phrasis 本指「说话的方式」，这个义项保留了那种形态：几个词被当作一整块话语握在一起，而不是逐个来数。

senses.title: A particular way of wording something
senses.definition: the words someone chooses in order to express an idea, considered as a style of expression
senses.definitionCN: 为表达某个想法而选用的词，被当作一种表达风格来看
senses.example: He turned the refusal into a polite phrase.
senses.exampleCN: 他把拒绝说成了一句客气话。
senses.why: Because a phrase is a fixed block of words, picking one block instead of another is exactly what wording means, so the noun slides from the block to the choice made among blocks.
senses.whyCN: 既然 phrase 是固定的一整块词，那么挑这一块而不挑那一块，正是「措辞」的意思，于是名词就从那一块滑到了「做选择」这件事上。

senses.title: A short passage in music
senses.definition: a short group of notes forming a unit in a melody, usually shaped so that a player or singer can breathe there
senses.definitionCN: 旋律中构成一个单位的短小音符组，通常处理成演奏者或歌者可以换气的地方
senses.example: The pianist shaped the opening phrase with great care.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家把开头的乐句处理得非常讲究。
senses.why: Music borrowed the term from speech: a melody is divided into breath-sized units the way a sentence is divided into word groups, so the same noun serves both arts.
senses.whyCN: 音乐从言语那里借来这个术语：旋律被分成一口气大小的单位，正如句子被分成词组，于是同一个名词同时服务于两种艺术。

senses.title: To express something in chosen words
senses.definition: to choose the words for a question, statement, or request, especially in order to control how it is received
senses.definitionCN: 为问题、陈述或请求挑选用词，尤指为了控制别人接收它的方式
senses.example: She phrased the question so that no one felt accused.
senses.exampleCN: 她把问题问得很讲究，没有人觉得是在受指责。
senses.why: English often turns a way of speaking into the act of speaking that way, so the noun for a word-block became the verb for arranging words with care.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把「一种说法」变成「按那种说法去说」的动作，于是指词块的名词就成了「仔细安排用词」的动词。

intro.en: Phrase goes back to a Greek noun for speech and style, and reached English through Latin and French as a name for a group of words.
intro.cn: phrase 可追到希腊语中表示言语与文风的名词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语，用来指一组词。

items.en: The verb phrazein meant to point out, declare, or tell, and it supplied the idea of putting a thought into speech.
items.cn: 动词 phrazein 意为指出、宣告、讲述，提供了「把想法说成话」这一观念。

items.en: The noun phrasis meant speech, manner of speaking, or style, and it named the way a thing was put into words.
items.cn: 名词 phrasis 意为言语、说话方式、文风，指一件事被说成话的方式。

items.en: Latin borrowed phrasis as a learned noun for wording and expression, and used it mainly in grammar and rhetoric.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 phrasis，作为表示措辞与表达的书卷名词，主要用于语法与修辞。

items.en: French phrase named both a group of words and a turn of speech, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 phrase 同时指一组词和一种说法，英语在十六世纪把它借了过来。

items.en: English kept the word-group sense, added the musical sense, and turned the noun into a verb for choosing words.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了「词组」义，添上音乐义，又把名词转为表示挑词造句的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group runs along the phras- stem and its derivatives; the near-meaning group gathers words for fixed expressions and for wording.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 phras- 词干及其派生词排列；近义组收表示固定表达与措辞的词。

entries.definition: Built on a phrase, especially in the term phrasal verb.
entries.definitionCN: 由短语构成，尤用于「短语动词」这一术语。

entries.definition: The way words are put together in speech or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 说话或写作中把词组织起来的方式。

entries.definition: To express someone else's meaning in different words.
entries.definitionCN: 用不同的话转述别人的意思。

entries.definition: The particular way a person or group uses words.
entries.definitionCN: 某人或某群体特有的用词方式。

entries.definition: A word or group of words used to convey an idea.
entries.definitionCN: 用来表达某个意思的词或词组。

entries.definition: A fixed group of words whose meaning cannot be guessed from the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 含义无法由各词直接推出的固定词组。

entries.definition: The words chosen for a statement, letter, or document.
entries.definitionCN: 为一段话、一封信或一份文件选用的词句。

entries.definition: A group of words with its own subject and verb, forming part of a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 带有自己的主语和动词、构成句子一部分的一组词；分句。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from a Greek noun for speech, and its whole family keeps circling the act of putting words together.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自希腊语中表示言语的名词，它的整个词族都绕着「把词组织起来」这个动作转。

normal.en: Greek phrasis meant manner of speaking, so a phrase is a piece of speech cut to a size you can hold in one breath.
normal.cn: 希腊语 phrasis 意为说话方式，所以短语是被切到「一口气能拿住」那么大的一块话。

normal.en: Paraphrase adds the Greek prefix para-, beside, to phrase: the same meaning is placed beside the original in other words.
normal.cn: paraphrase 在 phrase 前加希腊语前缀 para-（在旁边）：同一个意思被用别的话放在原文旁边。

normal.en: A phrasal verb is a verb plus one or two small words, and the whole group behaves like a single verb.
normal.cn: 短语动词是一个动词加一两个小词，整组词像单个动词那样使用。

normal.en: The verb phrase means to choose the words, so a carefully phrased letter is one whose wording was reworked.
normal.cn: 动词 phrase 意为挑选用词，所以「措辞谨慎的信」就是文字被反复改过的信。

normal.en: Music uses the same noun for a short melodic unit, because a melody is breathed through in units like a sentence.
normal.cn: 音乐用同一个名词指短小的旋律单位，因为旋律也像句子一样按单位换气。

abstract.en: A phrase is a handful of words tied together, small enough to lift and large enough to carry one idea.
abstract.cn: 短语是一把被捆在一起的词，小到能拿起来，大到能装下一个意思。

abstract.en: Wording and phrased are the same insight twice: first the block of words, then the hand that arranged it.
abstract.cn: 措辞与「措辞过」是同一个洞见的两面：先是那一块词，然后是安排它的那只手。

abstract.en: When a melody is phrased well, the listener hears speech with the words taken out.
abstract.cn: 当一段旋律被处理得当时，听者听到的是抽掉了词的言语。

examples.en: The phrase in brackets can be left out.
examples.cn: 括号里的那个短语可以省略。

examples.en: He phrased the refusal so gently that nobody felt hurt.
examples.cn: 他把拒绝说得十分委婉，没有人觉得受伤。

examples.en: The opening phrase of the sonata rises like a question.
examples.cn: 奏鸣曲开头的乐句像一句问话那样升起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗瑞兹」——说话像一串串珠子，一串就是一短语，记住 phrase。

root: 希腊语 phrazein（说出、宣告）派生 phrasis（言语、说法），经拉丁语 phrasis 与古法语 phrase 进入英语，核心是「被说成话的一组词」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a few words held together as one block; from that block come a way of wording, a musical unit, and the act of choosing words.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是几个词被握成一整块；由这一块长出措辞方式、音乐单位，以及挑词造句的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few word tiles threaded on a string and hung in the middle of a sentence.
core.cn: 核心意象：几块写着单词的小木牌被细线串起，挂在句子中间，像一串可以整块取下的珠子。

branches.en: a chalk circle drawn around three words on a blackboard
branches.cn: 黑板上被粉笔圈住的三个词

branches.en: a letter rewritten until the refusal sounds kind
branches.cn: 一封信改到拒绝听起来也不刺人

branches.en: a melody lifting at the end of its first small unit
branches.cn: 旋律在第一个小段落末尾扬起

branches.en: a speaker pausing to choose the softer word
branches.cn: 说话人停下来挑一个更软和的词

branches.en: a sentence assembled from ready-made blocks
branches.cn: 用现成的词块拼出的一句话

intro.en: The word is carried by a Greek verb and noun for speech, a Latin borrowing, and the English endings that build its family.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示言语的希腊语动词与名词、一次拉丁语借入，以及构成其词族的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as phrasis, so the Latin entry is a learned loan rather than a native Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语名词借作 phrasis，所以这里列出的拉丁词是书卷借词，而非拉丁本土词根。

items.meaning: a group of words, a turn of speech
a word group or a musical unit

definition_zh: 新近；最近；刚刚；以新的方式
definition_en: a short time ago, and also used before a past participle to show that something has just been made or has just become a certain way
core_image: 一扇刚刷完漆的门，漆还没干透，手指一碰就留下印记
scene: 校门口的牌子刚挂上去，油漆还带着光，孩子们围着它读上面的班级名。 The newly opened library stands where the old bus stop used to be.
sceneCN: 这里 newly 是「新近、刚刚」（第 1 个义项：不久前发生）；句意为刚开放的图书馆建在原来公交站的位置。图中可辨识物件：新漆的牌子、旧站牌的铁杆。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 novus 经古法语进入英语，义为「新奇；新奇事物」
由前缀 re- 加 new 构成，义为「更新；续订」

senses.title: A short time ago
senses.definition: recently, in the short period just before now
senses.definitionCN: 最近，在过去不久的短短一段时间里
senses.example: The newly painted wall still smells of fresh paint.
senses.exampleCN: 刚刷过漆的墙还带着新漆的味道。
senses.why: New supplies the idea of something fresh, and the adverb ending turns that freshness into a statement about when it arrived.
senses.whyCN: new 提供「崭新」的底色，副词词尾把这份崭新变成对时间的说明：它是什么时候到来的。

senses.title: In a fresh or different way
senses.definition: in a way that is new, fresh or different from what came before
senses.definitionCN: 以一种新的、与以往不同的方式
senses.example: She arranged the room newly, with the desk facing the window.
senses.exampleCN: 她重新布置了房间，让书桌朝向窗户。
senses.why: Once the adverb names freshness, it can describe the manner of an action, not only the moment when it happened.
senses.whyCN: 副词一旦表示「新鲜」，就不只能说明事情发生在什么时候，也能说明它是怎么做的。

senses.title: Recently made or newly become
senses.definition: used before a past participle to mean recently made, chosen or changed into that state
senses.definitionCN: 用在过去分词前，表示最近被做成、选出或变成某种状态
senses.example: The newly elected mayor promised to repair every street in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 新当选的市长承诺修好区里的每一条街。
senses.why: Placed in front of a participle, the adverb squeezes a whole clause about a recent change into two words.
senses.whyCN: 放在分词前面时，这个副词把一个关于「最近发生变化」的完整从句压缩成两个词。

intro.en: Newly is the adjective new plus the Old English adverb ending that became modern -ly, and the pair has meant both recently and in a new way.
intro.cn: newly 是形容词 new 加上演变为现代 -ly 的古英语副词词尾，这个组合既表示「最近」，也表示「以新的方式」。

items.en: A root meaning new is widely reconstructed, though the starred form is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 表示「新」的词根一般重构为 *newo-，带星号的形式是重构，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Nīwe meant new and supplied the adjective from which the adverb was built.
items.cn: nīwe 意为「新的」，是构成这个副词的那个形容词。

items.en: The ending -līce turned adjectives into adverbs of manner and is the ancestor of modern -ly.
items.cn: -līce 把形容词变成方式副词，是现代 -ly 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English wrote the adverb as newliche or newly and kept the sense of recently.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个副词写作 newliche 或 newly，保留了「最近」的意思。

items.en: Modern English shortened the ending and extended newly to combinations such as newly built and newly elected.
items.cn: 现代英语把词尾简化，并把 newly 扩展到 newly built、newly elected 这类组合中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on new and its adverb ending; the near-meaning group gathers words that also point to a time just before now.
note.cn: 形近组收以 new 及副词词尾构成的词；近义组收同样指向「就在不久前」的词。

entries.definition: Recently made or not existing before; the adjective behind newly.
entries.definitionCN: 新近制成或以前不存在的；newly 背后的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being new, or a new thing.
entries.definitionCN: 新奇的性质；新奇的事物。

entries.definition: To make something new again or to extend it.
entries.definitionCN: 使重新变新；更新或续订。

entries.definition: A person who married a short time ago.
A short time ago; the most neutral partner of newly.
entries.definitionCN: 不久前；newly 最中性的对应词。

entries.definition: In a newly made or newly done way.
entries.definitionCN: 以刚做好、刚完成的方式。

entries.definition: In the recent past, often with a repeated action.
entries.definitionCN: 近来；常与反复发生的动作连用。

entries.definition: A very short moment ago; more informal than newly.
entries.definitionCN: 刚刚；比 newly 更口语。

normalIntro.en: The word pairs new with an old adverb ending, and its family keeps returning to freshness, recent change and the manner of doing something.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把 new 与一个古老的副词词尾配在一起，词族反复回到新鲜、近期的变化以及做事的方式。

normal.en: new plus the adverb ending gives newly: in a new way, or a short time ago.
normal.cn: new 加上副词词尾就是 newly：以新的方式，或者不久前。

normal.en: The Old English ending -līce is the same one behind friendly and lovely.
normal.cn: 古英语词尾 -līce 也是 friendly、lovely 背后的那个词尾。

normal.en: newly usually stands right next to the word it changes, as in newly built or newly elected.
normal.cn: newly 通常紧挨着它修饰的词，如 newly built、newly elected。

normal.en: The -ly in friendly belongs to an adjective, while the -ly in newly makes a true adverb.
normal.cn: friendly 的 -ly 属于形容词，而 newly 的 -ly 构成真正的副词。

normal.en: In news writing, newly is more formal than just or recently.
normal.cn: 在新闻写作中，newly 比 just 或 recently 更正式。

abstract.en: Freshness is not only a quality; it is also a timestamp, and the adverb records both.
abstract.cn: 新鲜不只是一种性质，它还是一个时间戳，而这个副词把两者都记了下来。

abstract.en: A coat of paint that is still wet tells you the change happened moments ago.
abstract.cn: 一层还没干的漆，告诉你改变就发生在片刻之前。

abstract.en: Newly is the sound of something still settling into its new shape.
abstract.cn: newly 是某样东西还在适应新形状时发出的声响。

examples.en: The newly opened library stands where the old bus stop used to be.
examples.cn: 刚开放的图书馆建在原来公交站的位置。

examples.en: A newly hired teacher gets a week of training before classes begin.
examples.cn: 新聘的老师在开课之前要接受一周培训。

examples.en: The room looked newly cleaned, with every shelf empty.
examples.cn: 房间像是刚打扫过，每个架子都空着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「牛利」——新来的牛很顺利，刚上岗就干活；记住 newly 是「新近、刚刚」。

root: 古英语 nīwe（新的）加副词词尾 -līce 构成 nīwlice，后简化为 newly；与拉丁语 novus 同出原始印欧语的「新」词根，属远亲。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is freshness in time; the senses then split into the recent moment, the new manner, and the participle use for recent change.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是时间上的新鲜；义项由此分成「最近的时刻」「新的方式」，以及用于近期变化的分词搭配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door with paint still wet, so its newness can be felt at a touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇漆还没干的门，新不新，用手一碰就知道。

branches.en: a sign put up this morning
branches.cn: 今早才挂上的牌子

branches.en: furniture moved into a different pattern
branches.cn: 家具被摆成另一种格局

branches.en: a mayor taking the oath for the first time
branches.cn: 第一次宣誓就职的市长

branches.en: the same freshness applied to time and to manner
branches.cn: 同一份「新」，既用于时间，也用于方式

branches.en: a changed arrangement and a changed title
branches.cn: 被改动的布置与被换掉的职位

intro.en: The word is built from the adjective for new and an Old English adverb ending, with a few Latin cousins arriving through the same old root.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「新」的形容词和一个古英语副词词尾构成，另有一些拉丁远亲来自同一个古老词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin novus shares the same reconstructed root for new and supplies several formal English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus 与「新」共享同一个重构词根，并为英语提供了一些正式词汇。

items.meaning: recently made or not existing before

items.example: the novelty of a new toy

definition_zh: 吸引；使参与；雇用
definition_en: to attract and hold attention, to take part in something, or to employ someone
core_image: 故事讲到一半，所有孩子都往前探着身子
scene: 这个故事吸引了所有孩子的注意力。 The story engaged the attention of every child.
sceneCN: 这里 engage 是「吸引」（第 1 个义项：抓住并保持注意力）；句意：这个故事吸引了所有孩子的注意力。

senses.title: To attract and hold attention
senses.definition: to attract someone's interest so that they stay involved
senses.definitionCN: 吸引某人的兴趣并使其持续投入
senses.example: The story engaged the attention of every child.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事吸引了所有孩子的注意力。
senses.why: The old sense of pledging oneself survives as giving one's attention fully to something.
senses.whyCN: 古代表明承诺的含义保留下来，表现为把注意力完全交给某事。

senses.title: To take part in an activity
senses.definition: to become involved in an activity or discussion
senses.definitionCN: 参与某项活动或讨论
senses.example: The students engaged in a debate.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们参与了一场辩论。
senses.why: To engage is to commit oneself, so joining an activity is a form of pledge.
senses.whyCN: engage 意为投入自己，因此加入活动是一种承诺形式。

senses.title: To employ or hire someone
senses.definition: to arrange for someone to work for you for a time
senses.definitionCN: 安排某人为你工作一段时间
senses.example: They engaged a lawyer for the case.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为这个案子聘请了一位律师。
senses.why: Hiring is a formal commitment between two parties, so the pledge sense returns.
senses.whyCN: 雇用是双方之间正式的承诺，因此承诺义又回来了。

intro.en: Engage comes from Old French engagier, to pledge or bind by promise.
intro.cn: engage 来自古法语 engagier，意为以承诺作担保或约束。

items.en: Gage means a pledge, and engagier means to pledge.
items.cn: gage 意为抵押、担保，engagier 意为作担保。

items.en: English borrows engage with the sense of pledging oneself.
items.cn: 英语借入 engage，表示把自己投入承诺。

items.en: The word gains senses of hiring and taking part.
items.cn: 这个词获得雇用与参与的含义。

items.en: Engage becomes common for holding attention.
items.cn: 十九世纪，engage 常用来表示吸引注意力。

items.en: The word covers attention, involvement, and employment.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词涵盖注意力、参与和雇用。

note.en: Engage is to attract or involve; attract pulls interest, and participate means to take part.
note.cn: engage 是吸引或使投入，attract 拉来兴趣，participate 意为参加。

entries.definition: an arrangement to do something or a promise to marry
attractive and interesting
busy, involved, or promised in marriage
to pull interest toward something
to include or make someone part of something
to take part in an activity

normalIntro.en: Engage means to draw someone in, whether attention, activity, or a job.
normalIntro.cn: engage 意为把人带入，无论是注意力、活动还是工作。

normal.en: The story engaged every child.
normal.cn: 故事吸引了每个孩子。

normal.en: Students engage in debate.
normal.cn: 学生参与辩论。

normal.en: They engaged a lawyer.
normal.cn: 他们聘请了律师。

normal.en: An engaging speaker holds attention.
normal.cn: engaging speaker 抓住注意力。

normal.en: Disengage means to pull away.
normal.cn: disengage 意为退出。

abstract.en: Picture children leaning forward during a story.
abstract.cn: 想象听故事时往前探身的孩子。

abstract.en: See a handshake sealing a promise.
abstract.cn: 想象握手确认承诺。

abstract.en: Think of gears locking together and turning.
abstract.cn: 想象齿轮咬合转动。

examples.en: The story engaged the attention of every child.
examples.cn: 这个故事吸引了所有孩子的注意力。

examples.en: The students engaged in a debate.
examples.cn: 学生们参与了一场辩论。

examples.en: They engaged a lawyer for the case.
examples.cn: 他们为这个案子聘请了一位律师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因给吉」——把注意力「给」出去，就是投入；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 engagier，来自 gage（抵押、担保），意为作出承诺。

sensesIntro.en: The word links holding attention, joining an activity, and making a formal hire.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词连接抓住注意力、加入活动，以及正式聘用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pledge that draws a person fully in.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一个人完全拉进来的承诺。

branches.en: The base sense is attracting and holding attention.
branches.cn: 基本义是吸引并保持注意力。

branches.en: Involvement turns attention into participation.
branches.cn: 投入把注意力变成参与。

branches.en: A formal hire is a pledge of work.
branches.cn: 正式聘用是一种工作承诺。

branches.en: Interest and activity reinforce each other.
branches.cn: 兴趣与活动互相强化。

branches.en: Both participation and employment are commitments.
branches.cn: 参与和雇用都是承诺。

intro.en: Engage carries the old French root gage, meaning a pledge.
intro.cn: engage 带着古法语词根 gage，意为担保、承诺。

latinIntro.en: Engage is Germanic through French; it has no direct Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: engage 经法语来自日耳曼语，没有直接的拉丁词根。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 开启 engage。

items.example: Gage is the root of engage.
items.exampleCN: gage 是 engage 的词根。

items.example: Engage a lawyer means employ one.
items.exampleCN: engage a lawyer 意为聘请律师。

definition_zh: 坦率地说；坦白地
definition_en: in an honest and direct way
core_image: 说话人放下客套，直接把真实想法摆在桌上
scene: 坦率地说，这个想法行不通。 Frankly, the idea will not work.
sceneCN: 这里 frankly 是「坦率地说」（第 1 个义项）；句意：坦率地说，这个想法行不通。

senses.title: To speak honestly
senses.definition: used to say that you are being honest
senses.definitionCN: 用来表明自己说的是实话
senses.example: Frankly, the idea will not work.
senses.exampleCN: 坦率地说，这个想法行不通。
senses.why: This is the basic honesty adverb.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的坦诚副词义项。

senses.title: In a direct way
senses.definition: in a direct way that hides nothing
senses.definitionCN: 不隐藏地、直接地
senses.example: She spoke frankly about her fears.
senses.exampleCN: 她坦率地谈了自己的恐惧。
senses.why: The adverb also describes how someone acts.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词也描述人的行为方式。

intro.en: Frankly is frank plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: frankly 是 frank 加上副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Francus meant free.
items.cn: francus 意为自由的。

items.en: Franc meant free and open.
items.cn: franc 意为自由而开放。

items.en: English borrowed frank.
items.cn: 英语借入 frank。

items.en: Frankly marked honest speech.
items.cn: frankly 用来标记坦诚的言语。

items.en: It opened sentences in conversation.
items.cn: 它常出现在对话句首。

note.en: Frankly is compared with similar-looking words and with honesty words.
note.cn: 把 frankly 与形近词以及表示诚实的词作比较。

entries.definition: honest and direct
the quality of being frank
a country in Europe
in a truthful way
without hiding anything
in a clear and direct way

normalIntro.en: Frankly means no mask and no detour.
normalIntro.cn: frankly 表示不戴面具、不绕弯子。

normal.en: Frankly, the idea will not work.
normal.cn: 坦率地说，这个想法行不通。

normal.en: She spoke frankly about her fears.
normal.cn: 她坦率地谈了自己的恐惧。

normal.en: Frankly speaking, we need more time.
normal.cn: 坦率地说，我们需要更多时间。

normal.en: He frankly admitted the mistake.
normal.cn: 他坦承了这个错误。

normal.en: Quite frankly, I was surprised.
normal.cn: 老实说，我很惊讶。

abstract.en: Frankly is honesty with the door open.
abstract.cn: frankly 是敞着门的诚实。

abstract.en: A plain word can save a long talk.
abstract.cn: 一句直话能省去长谈。

abstract.en: Truth spoken kindly travels further.
abstract.cn: 善意说出的真话走得更远。

examples.en: Frankly, the idea will not work.
examples.cn: 坦率地说，这个想法行不通。

examples.en: She spoke frankly about her fears.
examples.cn: 她坦率地谈了自己的恐惧。

examples.en: He frankly admitted the mistake.
examples.cn: 他坦承了这个错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: frank（坦率的）加 -ly 变副词：不加掩饰地说，就是 frankly（坦率地说）。

root: 由 frank（坦率的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，核心义「不掩饰地」。

sensesIntro.en: Frankly means honestly or in a direct way.
sensesIntro.cn: frankly 意为坦率地说或直率地。

core.en: Speech with the mask removed.
core.cn: 摘下面具的言语。

branches.en: He states the truth at once.
branches.cn: 他立刻说出实情。

branches.en: She talks about fears openly.
branches.cn: 她公开谈论恐惧。

branches.en: The sentence opens with honesty.
branches.cn: 句子以坦诚开头。

branches.en: Honesty and openness are one stance.
branches.cn: 诚实与开放是同一种姿态。

branches.en: Direct speech shortens the road.
branches.cn: 直白的言语缩短了路。

intro.en: Frankly belongs to the frank family of honesty words.
intro.cn: frankly 属于 frank 这一诚实词族。

latinIntro.en: Frankly comes from Latin francus, free, through French.
latinIntro.cn: frankly 经由法语来自拉丁语 francus（自由的）。

definition_zh: 到…上面；向…之上；转到（话题）；发觉（线索）
definition_en: moving to a position on the surface of something; also used for boarding, for turning to a new subject, and for being on the track of something
core_image: 一只手把杯子从一张桌子提起，又稳稳放到另一张桌子上
scene: 厨房里，端着热汤的人侧身走过，把碗从灶台挪到餐桌中央。 He lifted the hot pot onto the middle of the table.
sceneCN: 这里 onto 是「到…上面」（第 1 个义项：移动到某物的表面之上）；句意是他把热锅端到桌子中央。画面是灶台、餐桌与冒着热气的锅。

pos.zh: 到…上面；向…之上；转到（话题）；发觉（线索）

derivatives.zh: 与 onto 同样由「介词加 to」构成，义为「到…里面」
由 on 与 to 演变而来的古旧形式，义为「到；向」
由 there 与 on 复合而成的正式副词，义为「在其上」

senses.title: To a position on a surface
senses.definition: moving so as to be on the surface of something or supported by it
senses.definitionCN: 移动之后位于某物表面之上，或由它支撑
senses.example: He lifted the hot pot onto the middle of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他把热锅端到桌子中央。
senses.why: Onto is on plus to, so it keeps both the direction of to and the contact of on: the movement ends on a surface.
senses.whyCN: onto 由 on 加 to 构成，同时保留 to 的「去向」与 on 的「接触」，即移动终点落在某个表面上。

senses.title: Up to a vehicle or a raised place
senses.definition: used with verbs of climbing or boarding, to show getting on a vehicle, a horse or a higher place
senses.definitionCN: 与攀爬、乘坐类动词连用，表示登上交通工具、马匹或高处
senses.example: The boy climbed onto the roof to fetch the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩爬上屋顶去取球。
senses.why: A vehicle and a roof are surfaces raised above the ground, so the surface sense narrows to getting up on them.
senses.whyCN: 交通工具和屋顶都是高过地面的表面，于是「表面」义收窄为「登上它们」的动作。

senses.title: Concerning; starting to deal with
senses.definition: used with verbs such as move or get, to show that someone starts talking about or dealing with a new subject
senses.definitionCN: 与 move、get 等动词连用，表示开始谈论或处理一个新话题
senses.example: Let us move onto the next question before we run out of time.
senses.exampleCN: 趁时间还没用完，我们接着谈下一个问题吧。
senses.why: The picture of stepping from one surface to another is reused for stepping from one topic to the next, so progress becomes movement.
senses.whyCN: 「从一块表面踏到另一块」的画面被移用到话题之间，于是推进被说成移动。

senses.title: Aware of something hidden; on the track of
senses.definition: used in be onto something, meaning to have discovered something important or to suspect someone
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be onto something，表示发现了重要线索或对某人起了疑心
senses.example: The researchers may be onto a cheaper way of storing solar power.
senses.exampleCN: 这些研究者可能发现了储存太阳能的一种更便宜的办法。
senses.why: If a trail or a scent is imagined as a surface, finding it means standing on it, which is why discovery is phrased as being onto something.
senses.whyCN: 如果把踪迹或气味想象成一块表面，找到它就等于站到了上面，所以「发现」被说成 be onto something。

intro.en: Onto is a young preposition made by joining two older ones, and its written form appears only after on and to had long lived apart.
intro.cn: onto 是一个年轻的介词，由两个更古老的介词合并而成，它的书写形式在 on 与 to 分开使用很久之后才出现。

items.en: On came from Old English an, meaning in or upon, and it named contact and support.
items.cn: on 源自古英语 an，意为在…之中、在…之上，指接触与支撑。

items.en: To came from Old English to, meaning toward a place, and it named direction and a destination.
items.cn: to 源自古英语 to，意为朝某处，指方向与目的地。

items.en: Middle English kept on and to apart, and wrote on to as two words when movement and contact had to be shown at once.
items.cn: 中古英语把 on 与 to 分开使用，需要同时表示移动与接触时就写作 on to 两个词。

items.en: The single written form onto appears in the eighteenth century, generally considered a blending of the two words, though many writers still prefer on to.
items.cn: 一般认为单一拼写 onto 出现在十八世纪，由两个词合并而成，但不少作者仍偏向写作 on to。

items.en: Modern English uses onto for physical movement, for boarding, for a new topic and for being on the track of something.
items.cn: 现代英语用 onto 表示实体移动、登上交通工具、转向新话题，以及察觉到某事。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers prepositions built on the same on-plus-to pattern; the near-meaning group gathers words of position above or on something.
note.cn: 形近组收同样按「on 加 to」模式构成的介词；近义组收表示在某物之上或更高位置的词。

entries.definition: Built like onto from in plus to, meaning to a position inside.
entries.definitionCN: 与 onto 同样由 in 加 to 构成，意为到…里面。

entries.definition: An older form of to, formed with on or un; it looks close but is not the modern onto.
entries.definitionCN: to 的一种较古形式，由 on 或 un 构成；形近，但不是现代的 onto。

entries.definition: A formal adverb meaning on that or on it, built from there plus on.
entries.definitionCN: 正式副词，意为「在其上」，由 there 加 on 构成。

entries.definition: On or onto, especially in formal and literary use.
entries.definitionCN: 在…之上或到…之上，尤用于正式与文学语体。

entries.definition: On top of something.
In a higher position than something, without the idea of contact.
entries.definitionCN: 位置高于某物，不含接触之意。

entries.definition: Towards a higher place or position.

normalIntro.en: The word fuses contact with direction, and its family keeps the picture of a hand carrying something until it rests on a new surface.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把接触与方向合在一起，同族用法始终保留「一只手把东西搬过去，直到落在新表面上」的画面。

normal.en: Onto is on plus to, so it fuses contact with direction in one short word.
normal.cn: onto 是 on 加 to，用一个短词把接触与方向合在一起。

normal.en: Into follows the same pattern with in, which is why the two prepositions are usually learned together.
normal.cn: into 用 in 走同样的路子，所以这两个介词常被一起学。

normal.en: Boarding a bus or a horse falls under onto because both are raised surfaces.
normal.cn: 上公交车或上马都用 onto，因为二者都是高起的表面。

normal.en: Move onto a new topic borrows the physical step from one surface to another.
normal.cn: move onto a new topic 借用了从一块表面踏到另一块的动作。

normal.en: Hold onto keeps the contact and adds the effort of not letting go.
normal.cn: hold onto 保留接触之意，又加上「不松手」的用力。

abstract.en: Picture a cup lifted from a counter and set down on another table: the arc of the hand is the to, the landing is the on.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子从台面提起又落到另一张桌上：手的弧线是 to，落点是 on。

abstract.en: Every new subject is a new surface to stand on, which is why progress and conversation share one preposition.
abstract.cn: 每个新话题都是一块可站的新表面，所以推进与谈话共用同一个介词。

abstract.en: Being onto something means the trail is under your feet, even when nothing can be seen yet.
abstract.cn: be onto something 意味着踪迹已经在脚下，尽管此时还什么都看不见。

examples.en: He lifted the hot pot onto the middle of the table.
examples.cn: 他把热锅端到桌子中央。

examples.en: The boy climbed onto the roof to fetch the ball.
examples.cn: 男孩爬上屋顶去取球。

examples.en: The researchers may be onto a cheaper way of storing solar power.
examples.cn: 这些研究者可能发现了储存太阳能的一种更便宜的办法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「昂途」——昂首踏上路途，跨到上面去；onto 意为到…上面。

root: onto 是 on 与 to 在近代合并而成的介词：on 源自古英语，表接触与支撑；to 表方向与终点。一般认为这一拼写形式在十八世纪出现。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a movement that ends on a surface; the senses extend that landing to vehicles, to new topics and to the ground of a discovery.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一次以落在表面为终点的移动」；义项把这层落点扩展到交通工具、新话题，以及发现线索时脚下的落点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifting a cup from one table and setting it down on another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把杯子从一张桌子提起，又放到另一张桌上。

branches.en: a hot pot set down in the middle of a table
branches.cn: 热锅被放到桌子中央

branches.en: a boy pulling himself up to a roof
branches.cn: 男孩攀上屋顶

branches.en: a meeting turning from one question to the next
branches.cn: 会议从上一个问题转向下一个

branches.en: a trail that has not yet been confirmed
branches.cn: 尚未被确认的一条线索

branches.en: one movement, whether across a room or across an agenda
branches.cn: 同一种移动，或跨过一间屋子，或跨过一项议程

intro.en: The word is held together by two Old English prepositions and the compound they later formed, together with the parallel forms built the same way.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个古英语介词、它们后来合成的复合词，以及按同样方式构成的平行形式支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to a position on a surface

definition_zh: 铁轨；轨道；栏杆；扶手；铁路；怒斥
definition_en: one of the metal bars that a train runs on; a bar used for support or safety; the railway as a means of transport; to complain angrily
core_image: 一段刚抬到位的钢轨，卡进枕木上的扣件
scene: 站台上，工人把一段新钢轨抬到位，卡进枕木上的扣件。 The workers laid a new section of rail along the curve.
sceneCN: 这里 rail 是「铁轨」（第 1 个义项：火车行驶其上的金属轨条）；句意为工人们沿着转弯处铺下了一段新的钢轨。画面里可留意：抬起的钢轨、枕木、扣件。

pos.zh: 铁轨；轨道；栏杆；扶手；铁路
怒斥；抱怨（多用于 rail against）

derivatives.zh: rail 加 -ing，指由栏杆组成的一排扶手或围栏
rail 与 way 复合，指铁路及其系统
rail 与 road 复合，美式用法，指铁路或铁路公司

senses.title: A metal bar for trains
senses.definition: one of the long metal bars on which a train's wheels run
senses.definitionCN: 火车车轮在其上行驶的长金属条之一
senses.example: The workers replaced a section of rail.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们更换了一段铁轨。
senses.why: The word comes from the Latin word for a straight rule, and a straight bar laid on the ground is exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语表示直尺的词，而铺在地上的一根直条正合此意。

senses.title: A bar for support or safety
senses.definition: a bar fixed along stairs or an edge to hold on to
senses.definitionCN: 沿楼梯或边缘固定、供人抓握的横杆
senses.example: Hold the rail as you go down the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 下台阶时抓住扶手。
senses.why: A straight bar serves equally as a track for wheels and as a handhold for people, so one word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 一根直杆既可为车轮当轨道，也可供人抓握，因此同一个词涵盖两者。

senses.title: The railway as transport
senses.definition: the railway system considered as a way of carrying people or goods
senses.definitionCN: 把人和货物运走的铁路系统
senses.example: They sent the goods by rail.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用铁路运送货物。
senses.why: By rail means by way of the rails, a common English habit of naming a transport system after its track.
senses.whyCN: by rail 意为经由铁路，这是英语常把交通系统以其轨道命名的习惯。

senses.title: To complain angrily
senses.definition: to speak angrily and at length about something, usually in rail against
senses.definitionCN: 对某事愤怒而冗长地发言，通常用于 rail against
senses.example: He railed against the new rules for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他对着新规痛斥了十分钟。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different French word meaning to scold, and it happens to share the English spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自另一个意为斥责的法语词，只是碰巧与 rail 共用同一个英语拼写。

intro.en: Rail comes from the Latin word for a straight rule, through French; the sense of scolding arrived separately from another French verb and merged in spelling.
intro.cn: rail 经法语来自拉丁语表示直尺的词；斥责义则另从一个法语动词而来，在拼写上合流。

items.en: Regula meant a straight stick or a rule, the tool used to test whether a line is straight.
items.cn: regula 指直棍或尺，是检验一条线是否笔直的工具。

items.en: Reille named a bar or a rail, and it also meant a rule in the sense of a standard.
items.cn: reille 指横杆或栏杆，也指作为标准的规则。

items.en: English rail first named a bar of wood or metal, then the bars laid for wagons and trains.
items.cn: 英语的 rail 先指木条或金属条，后指为货车与火车铺设的轨条。

items.en: The verb to rail, meaning to scold, came from a different French verb and took the same spelling.
items.cn: 表示斥责的动词 rail 来自另一个法语动词，却采用了相同的拼写。

items.en: Modern English uses rail for tracks, for handrails, for the railway itself and for angry complaint.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rail 指轨道、扶手、铁路本身，以及愤怒的抱怨。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same bar; the near-meaning group gathers words for tracks and supports.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一根「杆」构成的形式；近义组收表示轨道与支撑物的词。

entries.definition: A fence or barrier made of rails.
entries.definitionCN: 由横杆构成的围栏或护栏。

entries.definition: A track and system for trains.
entries.definitionCN: 供火车行驶的轨道与系统。

entries.definition: The American word for a railway.
To control by rules, from the same Latin word for a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 按规则控制，来自同一个表示尺与规则的拉丁词。

entries.definition: The pair of rails on which a train runs.
entries.definitionCN: 火车行驶其上的那对钢轨。

entries.definition: A long straight piece of metal or wood.
The handrail at the side of stairs.
The carrying of people or goods from place to place.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或货物从一处运到另一处。

normalIntro.en: The word is a straight bar: laid down it becomes a track, raised up it becomes a handrail, and joined together it becomes a railway.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一根直杆：铺下来是轨道，竖起来是扶手，连起来是铁路。

normal.en: Rail comes from the Latin word for a rule, which is also why regulate means to control by rules.
normal.cn: rail 来自拉丁语表示尺与规则的词，这也是 regulate 表示「按规则管理」的由来。

normal.en: By rail is the fixed phrase for travelling or sending goods by train.
normal.cn: by rail 是乘火车或经铁路运送货物的固定说法。

normal.en: A hand rail and a stair rail are the same bar, one for the hand and one for the stairs.
normal.cn: hand rail 与 stair rail 是同一根杆，一个供手抓，一个装在楼梯上。

normal.en: Railway is British, railroad is American, and both join rail to a word for a way.
normal.cn: railway 是英式，railroad 是美式，两者都把 rail 与表示「路」的词连在一起。

normal.en: To rail against something is to scold it at length, a sense that arrived from another French verb.
normal.cn: to rail against 某事物是长时间地斥责它，这一义项来自另一个法语动词。

abstract.en: A single straight bar becomes a whole system of movement once it is laid in a line, which is how infrastructure works.
abstract.cn: 一根直杆一旦被一线铺开，就成了整套运动系统，基础设施正是这样运作的。

abstract.en: A rail guides a train and a rail guards a stair: the same object either directs or protects.
abstract.cn: 铁轨引导火车，扶手保护走下楼梯的人：同一件东西要么引导，要么守护。

abstract.en: To rail against the world is to demand that it follow a straight rule, and the world rarely does.
abstract.cn: 对世界怒斥，就是要求它遵循一条笔直的规则，而世界很少如此。

examples.en: The train slowed as it crossed the rusty rail.
examples.cn: 火车越过那段生锈的铁轨时慢了下来。

examples.en: Please hold the rail while the floor is wet.
examples.cn: 地面湿滑时请抓住扶手。

examples.en: Most of the coal was carried by rail.
examples.cn: 大部分煤是通过铁路运输的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐欧」——一根锐利的直杆一直伸向远方，记住 rail 是铁轨、栏杆。

root: 拉丁语 regula（直尺、规则）→ 古法语 reille（横杆）→ 英语 rail；同族有 railing、railway、railroad、regulate。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a straight bar; the senses divide into a train track, a handhold, the railway system, and a separate verb of scolding.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一根直杆」；义项分为火车轨道、扶手、铁路系统，以及另出一个表示斥责的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a new steel rail lifted into place and clipped to the sleepers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段新钢轨被抬到位，扣在枕木上。

branches.en: wheels running along a bright line
branches.cn: 车轮沿一条亮线前行

branches.en: a hand gripping a stair rail
branches.cn: 握住楼梯扶手的一只手

branches.en: coal loaded into a long train
branches.cn: 装进长长列车的煤

branches.en: a voice scolding a notice board
branches.cn: 对着公告板斥责的声音

branches.en: the single bar and the system built from many
branches.cn: 单根轨条与由许多轨条组成的系统

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing on the Latin word for a rule, with English endings that build fences, systems and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「尺、规则」之上的法语借词，加上构成围栏、系统与复合词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin regula also gave English rule and regulate, which keep the sense of a straight standard.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regula 还给英语送来了 rule 与 regulate，它们保留了「笔直标准」的意思。

definition_zh: 继续进行；前进；着手；推进；（法律）起诉；发出（古义）
definition_en: to continue or move forward, especially after a pause or as the next step
core_image: 一条路在岔口干等，绿灯亮起后脚步重新向前
scene: 演示暂停后，主持人拿起翻页笔。 The host said we may proceed to the next slide, and the screen changed as soon as the button was pressed.
sceneCN: 这里 proceed 是「继续进行、进入下一步」（第 1 个义项：停顿之后接着往下走）；句意：主持人说我们可以继续看下一张幻灯片，按钮一按屏幕就换了画面。图中可辨识物件：投影屏、翻页笔、讲台、水杯、听众；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 继续进行；前进；着手；推进；（法律）起诉

senses.title: Continue after a pause
senses.definition: to continue doing something after stopping or waiting
senses.definitionCN: 停止或等待之后继续做某事
senses.example: After a short break, we proceeded with the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 短暂休息后，我们继续开会。
senses.why: Latin procedere means 'go forward': pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'go'. The word assumes something has stopped and now resumes its motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 procedere 意为“向前走”：pro-“向前”加 cedere“走”。这个词假定某物曾停下，现在重新开始运动。

senses.title: Move forward physically
senses.definition: to move onward in space
senses.definitionCN: 在空间中向前移动
senses.example: The procession proceeded slowly down the street.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍沿街缓慢行进。
senses.why: This is the literal core: feet or wheels moving along a path. Everything abstract in English is borrowed from this simple forward motion.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的核心：脚或轮子沿路移动。英语里一切抽象义都从这个简单的向前运动借来。

senses.title: Begin or undertake an action
senses.definition: to start doing something as the next step
senses.definitionCN: 作为下一步开始做某事
senses.example: We will proceed to build the prototype.
senses.exampleCN: 我们将着手制作原型。
senses.why: Starting and continuing are close: the next step is both the end of waiting and the beginning of action. The infinitive after proceed marks what is undertaken.
senses.whyCN: 开始与继续很近：下一步既是等待的结束，也是行动的开始。proceed 后接不定式，标记着手的内容。

senses.title: Carry out a plan or process
senses.definition: to carry on with a plan, process, or procedure
senses.definitionCN: 继续推进计划、过程或程序
senses.example: The committee proceeded according to the rules.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会按规则推进。
senses.why: Institutions need a script: proceed means to follow the prescribed steps. The word becomes procedural, which is why procedure is its close relative.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要脚本：proceed 意为按既定步骤走。这个词变得程序化，所以 procedure 是它的近亲。

senses.title: Make progress
senses.definition: to advance toward a goal
senses.definitionCN: 朝目标推进
senses.example: The project is proceeding well.
senses.exampleCN: 项目进展顺利。
senses.why: Forward motion becomes achievement: if the path advances, the work advances. English uses the same metaphor for time, work, and journeys.
senses.whyCN: 向前运动变成成就：路推进，工作就推进。英语用同一个隐喻说时间、工作与旅程。

senses.title: Go on to the next item
senses.definition: in formal speech, to move to the next topic or stage
senses.definitionCN: 正式讲话中，进入下一个话题或阶段
senses.example: Let us proceed to the second question.
senses.exampleCN: 让我们进入第二个问题。
senses.why: Meetings rank items in order. Proceed is the verbal signal that one item is closed and the next opened, a procedural gate rather than a physical one.
senses.whyCN: 会议把议题排序。proceed 是“上一项已关、下一项已开”的口头信号，是程序的关口而非物理关口。

senses.title: Take legal action against
senses.definition: to start or continue a legal action against someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人开始或继续法律诉讼
senses.example: The company proceeded against the supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 公司对供应商提起诉讼。
senses.why: Law is a path with formal steps: filing, hearing, judgment. To proceed against someone is to set that machinery in motion.
senses.whyCN: 法律是一条有正式步骤的路：提交、听证、判决。proceed against 某人，就是启动这套机器。

senses.title: Come forth or issue from (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to originate or come out from a source
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：从某个源头产生或出来
senses.example: Light proceeds from the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 光来自太阳。
senses.why: The Latin verb could mean 'come out of'. English kept this for a time: what proceeds from a source moves out of it. Modern usage prefers arise or issue.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词可指“从……出来”。英语保留过一阵：proceed from 某源，就是从它里面出来。现代多用 arise 或 issue。

senses.title: (Of an event) go forward
senses.definition: of an event or plan, to take place as arranged
senses.definitionCN: 事件或计划按安排进行
senses.example: The wedding will proceed despite the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管下雨，婚礼仍将举行。
senses.why: An event is treated as an object on a path: it can be stopped, delayed, or allowed to proceed. The word grants permission to the future.
senses.whyCN: 事件被当作路上的物件：它可以被停下、推迟，或被允许 proceed。这个词是在给未来发放许可。

intro.en: Proceed is a pure motion word: pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'go'. English borrowed it in the late 14c. and then extended the walk into meetings, projects, and lawsuits.
intro.cn: proceed 是一个纯粹的运动词：pro-“向前”加 cedere“走”。英语在 14 世纪末借入，随后把这场行走扩展到会议、项目与诉讼。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'go forward, continue one's course'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“向前走、继续行程”。

items.en: From Latin procedere 'go forward, advance, come forth' = pro- 'forward' + cedere 'go, yield'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 procedere“向前走、推进、出现”= pro-“向前”+ cedere“走、让”。

items.en: cedere also gives cede, accede, concede, exceed, precede, and succeed. The base is about going or yielding, and the prefix pro- points the going forward.
items.cn: cedere 还生成 cede、accede、concede、exceed、precede、succeed。词基关乎走或让，前缀 pro- 把方向指向前。

items.en: The legal sense 'begin or carry on an action at law' develops, producing proceedings and procedure.
items.cn: 法律义“开始或继续诉讼”发展出来，产生 proceedings 与 procedure。

items.en: Modern English uses proceed for meetings, projects, and formal sequences, always with a sense of a path resumed.
items.cn: 现代英语用 proceed 指会议、项目与正式流程，始终带有“路径重新开始”的意味。

note.en: The first group shares the cedere root; the second is about verbs that also mean continuing or advancing.
note.cn: 第一组共享 cedere 词根，第二组看同样表示“继续”或“推进”的动词。

entries.definition: to come before. It uses prae- 'before' + cedere.
entries.definitionCN: 在……之前。它用 prae-“在前”+ cedere。

entries.definition: to come after; to achieve a goal. It is sub- 'under, next' + cedere.
entries.definitionCN: 随后；成功。它是 sub-“在其后”+ cedere。

entries.definition: a set of steps for doing something. It is proceed plus -ure.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的步骤。它是 proceed 加 -ure。

entries.definition: to keep doing something without stopping. It stresses duration, not direction.
entries.definitionCN: 不停顿地做下去。它强调持续，而非方向。

entries.definition: to move forward or make progress. It is closer to the physical sense of proceed.
entries.definitionCN: 向前移动或取得进展。它更接近 proceed 的物理义。

entries.definition: to develop toward a better state. It stresses improvement, not sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 朝更好状态发展。它强调改善，而非次序。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin cedere 'go', the pro- 'forward' prefix, the proceed/precede/succeed trio, and the legal use proceed against.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 cedere“走”、前缀 pro-“向前”、proceed/precede/succeed 三词，以及法律用法 proceed against。

normal.en: Cedere means 'go' and pro- means 'forward': proceed is to go forward.
normal.cn: cedere 意为“走”，pro- 意为“向前”：proceed 就是向前走。

normal.en: Precede is prae- plus cedere, 'go before'; succeed is sub- plus cedere, 'go next'. The prefix sets the position.
normal.cn: precede 是 prae- 加 cedere，“走在前面”；succeed 是 sub- 加 cedere，“接着走”。前缀定位置。

normal.en: To proceed assumes a pause: something stopped and now resumes. It is motion after a gap.
normal.cn: proceed 假定有停顿：某物停下，现在重启。它是间隙之后的运动。

normal.en: In meetings, proceed is a procedural gate: one item closes, the next opens.
normal.cn: 会议中，proceed 是程序关口：一项关闭，下一项开启。

normal.en: To proceed against someone is to start the legal machinery walking.
normal.cn: proceed against 某人，就是让法律机器开始行走。

abstract.en: Forward is both a direction and a value: progress borrows its authority from the geometry of motion.
abstract.cn: 向前既是方向也是价值：进步从运动的几何学借来权威。

abstract.en: Every procedure is a path made repeatable, so that anyone can walk it without knowing the ground.
abstract.cn: 每一种程序都是被做成可重复的路径，好让任何人都能走而不必认识地形。

abstract.en: Permission to proceed is permission to let time continue; a meeting pauses the world and then releases it.
abstract.cn: 允许 proceed，就是允许时间继续；会议暂停世界，再把它放行。

examples.en: Please proceed with your report.
examples.cn: 请继续你的报告。

examples.en: We proceeded to the next item on the agenda.
examples.cn: 我们进入议程的下一项。

examples.en: The firm proceeded against the contractor for breach of contract.
examples.cn: 公司以违约为由起诉承包商。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若细的”——扑过去，像细线一样一路向前 → proceed 前进、继续进行

root: 拉丁语 procedere“向前走”，由 pro-“向前”+ cedere“走”构成；同族有 cede、precede、succeed、exceed。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of proceed, all one walk. The walk can resume after a break, advance in space, start a task, follow a procedure, enter the next agenda item, or enter a courtroom.
sensesIntro.cn: proceed 的九个义项，都是同一场行走。这场行走可以在休息后重启、在空间中前进、开始一项任务、遵循程序、进入下一议题，或进入法庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: putting one foot in front of the other along a path.
core.cn: 核心意象：沿一条路一步步向前。

branches.en: RESUME: motion restarts after a pause, or an event is allowed to continue.
branches.cn: 重启：停顿后重新运动，或事件被允许继续。

branches.en: ADVANCE: physical forward movement becomes measurable progress.
branches.cn: 推进：物理的向前运动变成可测量的进展。

branches.en: NEXT STEP: the walk becomes a sequence of tasks or agenda items.
branches.cn: 下一步：行走变成任务或议程的序列。

branches.en: PROCEDURE: the path is scripted into repeatable steps.
branches.cn: 程序：路径被写成可重复的步骤。

branches.en: LAW AND SOURCE: proceed against starts legal machinery; the archaic sense comes forth from a source.
branches.cn: 法律与来源：proceed against 启动法律机器；古义指从源头出来。

intro.en: Proceed is a Latin verb. English adds -ing, -ure, and -al, and the root cedere also builds precede, succeed, exceed, and cede.
intro.cn: proceed 是拉丁动词。英语加 -ing、-ure、-al，词根 cedere 还构成 precede、succeed、exceed、cede。

latinIntro.en: Latin procedere 'go forward' sits beside cedere 'go, yield'. The family is directional: prae- gives precede, sub- gives succeed, pro- gives proceed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 procedere“向前走”旁边是 cedere“走、让”。这个词族是有方向的：prae- 生成 precede，sub- 生成 succeed，pro- 生成 proceed。

items.meaning: an action or piece of business; a legal step
records of a meeting; legal actions
an established way of doing something

latinEntries.meaning: to go forward, advance, come forth

definition_zh: 帮助；协助；援助；（体育）助攻；有助于
definition_en: to help someone do something, to give a sports assist, or to help a process happen more easily
core_image: 一双手从旁边扶住摇摇欲倒的车轮
scene: 修车铺里，学徒扶住倾斜的车轮，师傅腾出手来拧紧螺栓。 Two neighbours assisted the old man with his shopping.
sceneCN: 这里 assist 是「帮助、协助」（第 1 个义项：在具体事务上帮某人一把）；句意为「两位邻居帮老人拎了买的东西」。画面中有修车铺、扶住车轮的学徒与腾出手的师傅。

pos.zh: 动词：帮助；协助；援助；（体育）助攻；有助于

derivatives.zh: 由 assist 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「帮助；援助」
由 assist 加 -ant 构成，义为「助手；助理」
由 assist 加 -ive 构成，义为「辅助的；助力的」

senses.title: To help with a task
senses.definition: to help someone do something, especially by taking part in the work
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人做某事，尤指参与其中分担工作
senses.example: Two neighbours assisted the old man with his shopping.
senses.exampleCN: 两位邻居帮老人拎了买的东西。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to stand beside, and help begins with standing next to someone who needs it.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「站在旁边」，而帮助正是从站到需要的人身边开始的。

senses.title: A sports assist
senses.definition: in team sports, a pass or play that directly leads to a goal or score by another player
senses.definitionCN: 在团队运动中，直接促成另一名队员得分的一次传球或配合
senses.example: Her assist set up the winning goal.
senses.exampleCN: 她的助攻促成了制胜的一球。
senses.why: The helper stands beside the scorer and makes the final act possible without performing it.
senses.whyCN: 助攻者站在得分者旁边，让最后一击成为可能，却不亲自完成它。

senses.title: To help a process happen
senses.definition: to make a process work more easily or effectively, as a substance or condition
senses.definitionCN: 使某个过程更顺利或更有效，如某种物质或条件所起的作用
senses.example: A little walking assists digestion after a meal.
senses.exampleCN: 饭后稍走一走有助于消化。
senses.why: Here the helper is not a person but a condition that stands beside the process and supports it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的帮手不是人，而是一个站在过程旁边、给它支撑的条件。

intro.en: Assist comes from a Latin verb meaning to stand beside, and its family includes assist, assistance and assistant.
intro.cn: assist 来自一个意为「站在旁边」的拉丁动词，词族包括 assist、assistance 与 assistant。

items.en: The root 「*sta-」 meant 'to stand', and it lies behind Latin sistere and many standing words.
items.cn: 词根「*sta-」意为「站立」，拉丁语 sistere 以及许多表示站立的词都由它而来。

items.en: Sistere meant 'to cause to stand, take one's stand', and assistere added ad- 'to': to stand beside.
items.cn: sistere 意为「使站立、站定」，assistere 又加上 ad-「向」，即「站在旁边」。

items.en: Assistere was used for a person standing by to help, and for soldiers posted nearby.
items.cn: assistere 既用于站在一旁帮忙的人，也用于就近驻扎的士兵。

items.en: Old French assister kept the sense of standing by to give help.
items.cn: 古法语 assister 保留了「站在旁边给予帮助」的意思。

items.en: English assist first meant to be present with and support someone, then to take a share of the work.
items.cn: 英语里的 assist 最初指在场支持某人，后来指分担一部分工作。

items.en: Sports added the assist as a counted act, and medicine speaks of a drug assisting digestion.
items.cn: 体育把助攻变成可计数的行为，医学则说某种药有助于消化。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs close to assist in spelling but with other roots; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of helping and supporting.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写与 assist 接近但词根不同的动词；近义组收表示帮助与支持的动词。

entries.definition: To judge the value or quality of something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「评估、评定」，注意它与 assist 词源不同。

entries.definition: To be made up of particular parts.
To state something firmly and refuse to change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「坚持、坚决主张」。

entries.definition: To make it easier for someone to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人做某事变得更容易。

entries.definition: To give support or relief, especially in need.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指在需要时给予支持或救济。

entries.definition: To hold something up or give it strength.
To give help or support to a person or plan.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人或某个计划以帮助或支持。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow assist from a hand under a wheel to a counted pass, a helping drug and everyday aid.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子让 assist 从扶住车轮的手，走到一次记数的传球、帮上忙的药与日常的援手。

normal.en: Assist means to stand beside.
normal.cn: assist 的意思就是「站在旁边」。

normal.en: One hand under the wheel lets the other hand work.
normal.cn: 一只手扶住车轮，另一只手才能干活。

normal.en: A sports assist is a pass counted as help.
normal.cn: 体育助攻是一次被记成帮助的传球。

normal.en: A drug assists digestion by standing beside the process.
normal.cn: 药物站在消化的过程旁边，推一把。

normal.en: Assistant and assistance are the same stand-beside.
normal.cn: assistant 与 assistance 都是同一个「站旁边」。

abstract.en: Help begins with presence, not with doing the whole job.
abstract.cn: 帮助始于在场，而不是把整件事都做掉。

abstract.en: People, passes and medicines can all assist.
abstract.cn: 人、传球与药物都能 assist。

abstract.en: The helper makes the final act possible without taking it.
abstract.cn: 帮手让最后一击成为可能，却不把它拿走。

examples.en: Two neighbours assisted the old man with his shopping.
examples.cn: 两位邻居帮老人拎了买的东西。

examples.en: Her assist set up the winning goal.
examples.cn: 她的助攻促成了制胜的一球。

examples.en: A little walking assists digestion after a meal.
examples.cn: 饭后稍走一走有助于消化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿西斯」——阿西斯从旁边扶住倾斜的车轮，让师傅腾出手来：协助

root: assist 来自拉丁语 assistere「站在旁边」，由 ad-「向」加 sistere「站立」构成，词根可追到意为「站」的「*sta-」。它最初指站在某人身边给予支持，后来指分担一部分工作；体育把这种支持变成可计数的助攻；用在药物或条件上，则指「站在某个过程旁边，使它更顺利」。注意它与 assess（坐在旁边称量）词根不同：assist 是站，assess 是坐。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses all mean standing beside: helping with work, supplying the pass before a score, and supporting a bodily process.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都是「站在旁边」：帮着一块干活、在得分前送出传球，以及给身体过程以支撑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding a tilting wheel steady so another pair of hands can work.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手扶稳倾斜的车轮，让另一双手腾出来干活。

branches.en: THE PRESENCE LINE: help starts by standing next to someone.
branches.cn: 在场线：帮助从站到某人身边开始。

branches.en: THE PASS LINE: the helper makes the score possible.
branches.cn: 传球线：帮手让得分成为可能。

branches.en: THE PROCESS LINE: a condition stands beside a bodily process and eases it.
branches.cn: 过程线：某个条件站在身体过程旁边，让它顺利些。

branches.en: THE TEAM LINE: a helper and a scorer share one move.
branches.cn: 团队线：帮手与得分者共享同一个动作。

branches.en: THE RELIEF LINE: people and medicines both lighten a load.
branches.cn: 缓解线：人与药物都在减轻负担。

intro.en: Assist is a Latin verb; its family adds -ance, -ant and -ive, with the same standing-beside core.
intro.cn: assist 是拉丁动词，词族加 -ance、-ant 与 -ive，共享同一个「站在旁边」的核心。

latinIntro.en: The Latin standing verb sistere also gave resist and insist, which keep the idea of taking a stand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示站立的 sistere 还生出 resist 与 insist，它们都保留「站定立场」的意思。

items.meaning: the third person singular or plural noun
items.example: He assists at every home game.
items.exampleCN: 每场主场比赛他都在旁协助。

items.example: She is assisting with the survey.
items.exampleCN: 她正在协助做这项调查。

items.meaning: the past tense and past participle
items.exampleCN: 志愿者帮助了洪灾灾民。

items.example: The app has assistive reading tools.
items.exampleCN: 这款应用有辅助阅读的工具。

items.meaningCN: 在没有帮助的情况下完成的

latinEntries.example: They resisted the change for years.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 他们多年抵制这一变化。

latinEntries.meaning: to stand firmly on a point

definition_zh: 保证；保修；担保
definition_en: a firm promise that something will be done, or a promise to repair or replace goods
core_image: 店家在收据上写下一年保修的承诺
scene: 店家保证一年内免费维修。 The shop guarantees free repairs for a year.
sceneCN: 这里 guarantee 是「保证」（第 1 个义项）；句意：店家保证一年内免费维修。

senses.title: Firm promise
senses.definition: a formal promise that something will happen
senses.definitionCN: 对某事必定发生的正式承诺
senses.example: The shop guarantees free repairs for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 店家保证一年内免费维修。
senses.why: This is the general modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最通用的义项。

senses.title: Product warranty
senses.definition: a written promise to repair or replace a product
senses.definitionCN: 对产品修理或更换的书面承诺
senses.example: The phone is still under guarantee.
senses.exampleCN: 这部手机还在保修期内。
senses.why: Shops turned the promise into a document.
senses.whyCN: 商家把承诺变成了一纸凭证。

senses.title: Legal surety
senses.definition: a promise to pay another person's debt if they fail
senses.definitionCN: 在他人无法偿还时替其付款的承诺
senses.example: His uncle guaranteed the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他的叔叔为这笔贷款作了担保。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a pledge for another.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是为他人作保。

intro.en: Guarantee comes from Old French garantie, a pledge of protection, from garantir, to protect.
intro.cn: guarantee 来自古法语 garantie（保护性担保），源头是 garantir（保护）。

items.en: The root meant to protect or guard.
items.cn: 该词根意为保护、看守。

items.en: Garant meant a person who protects.
items.cn: garant 指提供保护的人。

items.en: Garantie meant a pledge.
items.cn: garantie 意为担保、保证。

items.en: Guarantee meant a promise of safety.
items.cn: guarantee 意为安全的承诺。

items.en: The word also named a product warranty.
items.cn: 这个词也指产品保修。

note.en: Guarantee is compared with look-alike words and words for promises.
note.cn: 把 guarantee 与形近词以及表示承诺的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who protects a place
help and advice
a person invited to visit
a statement that you will do something
to tell someone surely
a written authority or promise

normalIntro.en: Guarantee began as protection and now means a firm promise or a warranty.
normalIntro.cn: guarantee 原指保护，如今指坚定的承诺或保修凭证。

normal.en: We guarantee delivery by Friday.
normal.cn: 我们保证周五前送达。

normal.en: The watch has a two-year guarantee.
normal.cn: 这块表有两年保修。

normal.en: Hard work does not guarantee success.
normal.cn: 努力并不保证成功。

normal.en: Is the laptop still under guarantee?
normal.cn: 这台笔记本电脑还在保修期内吗？

normal.en: His father guaranteed the loan.

definition_zh: 背景；上下文；语境
definition_en: the situation or the words around something that help explain it
core_image: 一段话的左右两边，把中间那句托住
scene: 读到生词时，她先把整段话看一遍再猜意思。 You can guess the word from its context.

senses.title: Surrounding words
senses.definition: the words before and after a word that help fix its meaning
senses.definitionCN: 位于某词前后、帮助确定其含义的文字
senses.example: Read the whole sentence to get the context.
senses.exampleCN: 读整个句子来把握上下文。
senses.why: A word alone can point several ways, and its neighbours steady it.
senses.whyCN: 一个词单看可以有几种指向，邻居让它稳住。

senses.title: The situation around
senses.definition: the conditions and events that surround something
senses.definitionCN: 围绕某事的条件与事件
senses.example: The decision made sense in the context of that year.
senses.exampleCN: 放在那一年的背景下，这个决定是说得通的。
senses.why: Nothing happens in empty air, and the air explains it.
senses.whyCN: 没有事发生在真空里，周围的空气正好解释它。

senses.title: Setting for meaning
senses.definition: the general field in which an idea is understood
senses.definitionCN: 理解某个观念所依托的整体领域
senses.example: The word has a different force in a legal context.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词在法律语境里力度不同。
senses.why: The same sentence changes colour when the room around it changes.
senses.whyCN: 同一句话，周围的房间一换，颜色也变了。

intro.en: Context comes from Latin contexere, to weave together, built from com-, together, and texere, to weave.
intro.cn: context 来自拉丁语 contexere，意为编织在一起，由 com-（一起）与 texere（编织）构成。

items.en: Texere meant to weave cloth from separate threads.
items.cn: texere 意为把分开的线织成布。

items.en: Contexere meant to weave things into one joined whole.
items.cn: contexere 意为把事物织成一个相连的整体。

items.en: Contextus named the joining of a text as well as a fabric.
items.cn: contextus 既指织物的连接，也指文字的连缀。

items.en: French contexte named the connected body of a written work.
items.cn: 法语 contexte 指一篇文字相连的整体。

items.en: English context first meant the words around a passage.
items.cn: 英语 context 最初指一段话周围的文字。

items.en: The word has widened to mean any surrounding situation.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩大为指任何周围的处境。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin weaving base text-, and the meaning group names other ways of speaking about surroundings.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的编织词基 text-，近义组列出其他表示周边环境的说法。

normal.en: A frame tells you how to see the picture inside it.

abstract.en: Picture a lamp lighting the wall behind a small object.

definition_zh: 因此；遂；于是
definition_en: for this reason, or from this time
core_image: 从这一点出发，射出的一条因果线
scene: 路上结了冰，因此他们决定待在家里。 The roads were icy; hence they decided to stay home.

definition_zh: 态度；看法；姿势
definition_en: a way of thinking or feeling about something, or a bodily posture
core_image: 身体微微前倾，把立场写在姿态上
scene: 面试官问他对加班怎么看。 His relaxed attitude surprised the interviewer.
sceneCN: 这里 attitude 是「态度」（第 1 个义项：对事情的看法与姿态）；句意是他轻松的态度让面试官感到意外。

senses.title: Way of thinking
senses.definition: a settled way of thinking or feeling about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事较为固定的想法与感受
senses.example: His relaxed attitude surprised the interviewer.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻松的态度让面试官感到意外。
senses.why: Attitude came from Italian attitudine, 'aptness or posture', from Latin aptitudo 'fitness', so the mental sense grew out of a body set a certain way.
senses.whyCN: attitude 来自意大利语 attitudine「适宜、姿态」，其拉丁词源 aptitudo 意为「适合」，所以心里的看法是从身体的摆法长出来的。

senses.title: Bodily posture

senses.example: He stood in an attitude of prayer.
senses.exampleCN: 他摆出祈祷的姿势站着。
senses.why: The oldest sense was the body's pose, and this concrete use survives in literary description even though the mental sense now dominates.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是身体的摆法，尽管如今心里的看法占主流，这个具体义仍保留在文学描写中。

intro.en: Attitude is a word of fitness that began with the body and moved into the mind.

senses.why: The verb probably comes from the older sense of pricking or thrusting, and a blow with the fist is a thrust made with the whole arm.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词大概来自更早的「刺、戳」义，而用拳打人正是用整条手臂做出的一次戳击。

senses.title: To make a hole with a tool
senses.definition: to make a hole in paper, metal or leather with a sharp tool or machine
senses.definitionCN: 用尖锐工具或机器在纸、金属、皮革上打出孔洞
senses.example: The clerk punched a hole in my ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 职员在我的票上打了个孔。
senses.why: A punch is first a pointed tool driven through material, so the verb keeps the image of a small sharp point entering and leaving.
senses.whyCN: punch 最初指被压穿材料的尖头工具，因此动词保留了「一个尖点进入又穿出」的形象。

senses.title: A tool or machine that cuts holes
senses.definition: a tool or machine with a sharp end that cuts holes or stamps shapes into material
senses.definitionCN: 带尖头、能在材料上打孔或压出形状的工具或机器
senses.example: The workshop bought a new punch for the steel plates.
senses.exampleCN: 车间为钢板买了一台新冲床。
senses.why: The name of the tool outlives the act: what was once a hand-held point becomes a heavy machine, and both are still called a punch.
senses.whyCN: 工具的名字比动作更长寿：曾经的手持尖锥变成了沉重的机器，两者至今都叫 punch。

senses.title: Force or impact, in a blow or in words
senses.definition: the power to strike hard, whether of a blow, a drink or a remark
senses.definitionCN: 击打、饮品或言语带来的强烈力度与感染力
senses.example: Her closing sentence had real punch.
senses.exampleCN: 她结尾那句话很有冲击力。
senses.why: Something that hits hard leaves a mark, so the noun for the blow is used for whatever produces a similar jolt, including a line of argument.
senses.whyCN: 打得重的东西会留下痕迹，于是「一击」这个名词被用来指产生同样震动的东西，包括一句论证。

senses.title: A mixed drink of fruit juice and spirits
senses.definition: a drink made by mixing fruit juice, sugar and spirits, usually served in a large bowl
senses.definitionCN: 把果汁、糖与烈酒调在一起、通常盛在大碗里供应的饮品
senses.example: A bowl of punch stood at the end of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌子尽头摆着一碗潘趣酒。
senses.why: This sense is not related to the fist or the tool at all: it comes from Hindi panch, five, for a drink once mixed from five ingredients.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项与拳头、工具完全无关：它来自印地语 panch（五），因为这种饮品从前用五种配料调成。

intro.en: Punch has two separate histories that happen to share one spelling: the fist-and-hole word goes back through French to Latin pungere, to prick, while the drink comes from Hindi panch, five.
intro.cn: punch 有两条彼此无关的历史，只是恰好共用一个拼法：表示拳击与打孔的词经法语上溯到拉丁语 pungere（刺），而表示饮品的那条则来自印地语 panch（五）。

items.en: Pungere meant to prick or pierce, and it is the source of the Latin nouns for a point and for a pricking pain.
items.cn: pungere 意为刺、戳穿，是拉丁语中表示「尖点」与「刺痛」的名词的来源。

items.en: Punctum meant a prick or a point, literally something made by piercing, and it underlies puncture and punctual.
items.cn: punctum 意为刺痕或一点，字面就是「被戳出来的东西」，是 puncture 与 punctual 的来源。

items.en: Old French poinçon named an awl or a pointed tool, and the verb ponchonner meant to prick or stamp with it.
items.cn: 古法语 poinçon 指锥子一类尖头工具，动词 ponchonner 意为用它刺或冲压。

items.en: Middle English borrowed punch as a verb for pricking or perforating, and by the sixteenth century it also meant striking with the fist.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 punch 作动词，指刺穿、打孔；到十六世纪也指用拳头打。

items.en: The drink is a separate borrowing of the seventeenth century from Hindi panch, five, for a bowl mixed from five ingredients; it shares no root with the fist.
items.cn: 表示饮品的那条是十七世纪从印地语 panch（五）单独借入的，指用五种配料调成的一碗酒；它与拳头义毫无词根关系。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that rhyme with punch but are unrelated; the near-meaning group collects verbs for hitting and nouns for a blow.
note.cn: 形近组收与 punch 押韵但彼此无关的词；近义组收表示打击的动词与表示一击的名词。

entries.definition: A group of things gathered or tied together.
entries.definitionCN: 聚拢或扎在一起的一束东西。

entries.definition: The meal eaten in the middle of the day.
To squeeze a small fold of skin between finger and thumb.
entries.definitionCN: 用拇指与食指捏住一小块皮肤。

entries.definition: A large rounded stomach.
To strike someone or something with force.
To hit something deliberately, often with the hand or a weapon.
entries.definitionCN: 有意地用手或器械击打。

entries.definition: A quick short punch, especially in boxing.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指拳击中的快速短拳。

entries.definition: To hit something heavily, making a dull sound.

normalIntro.en: Two unrelated words wear the same spelling: one is a Latin point driven through material or into a face, the other is a five-part drink from India.
normalIntro.cn: 两个互不相干的词穿着同一个拼法：一个是把拉丁语的尖点压进材料或打进脸上的动作，另一个是来自印度、由五样东西调成的酒。

normal.en: Punch the verb goes back through French to Latin pungere, to prick, which is why a pointed tool and a fist blow share the word.
normal.cn: 动词 punch 经法语上溯到拉丁 pungere（刺），所以尖头工具与拳击共用一个词。

normal.en: Punctum, a point or prick, gives English puncture and punctual, both still about a small sharp point or an exact point in time.
normal.cn: punctum（点、刺痕）给英语带来 puncture 与 punctual，两者仍与尖点或准确的时间点有关。

normal.en: The punch that cuts paper is the oldest tool sense; the machine in a workshop grew from that hand-held point.
normal.cn: 在纸上打孔的 punch 是最早的工具义，车间里的机器正是从那个手持尖锥长出来的。

normal.en: Punch the drink is a different word from Hindi panch, five, named for five ingredients in one bowl.
normal.cn: 表示饮品的 punch 是另一个词，来自印地语 panch（五），因一碗里放五样配料而得名。

normal.en: Pack a punch and punch line both use the blow as a metaphor: something lands hard on the listener.
normal.cn: pack a punch 与 punch line 都把这一击当比喻：有什么东西重重落在听者身上。

abstract.en: One spelling, two histories: a point that pierces, and five things stirred in a bowl.
abstract.cn: 一个拼法，两段历史：一个刺穿的尖点，和五样在碗里搅匀的东西。

abstract.en: A punch is short and concentrated, which is why the word also means the force that a sentence can carry.
abstract.cn: 一拳短促而集中，所以这个词也用来指一句话能带出的力量。

abstract.en: Words that land hardest usually contain the fewest of them.
abstract.cn: 最能打中人的话，往往用的词最少。

examples.en: He punched the door in frustration.
examples.cn: 他懊恼地一拳打在门上。

examples.en: The guard punched my ticket twice.
examples.cn: 检票员在我的票上打了两个孔。

examples.en: They served lemonade and fruit punch in the garden.
examples.cn: 他们在花园里供应柠檬水和水果潘趣酒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「乓啷」——拳头一出，乓啷一声落在沙袋上；记住 punch 是出拳，也别忘了那碗五种料调成的潘趣酒。

root: 两条互不相干的来源：一为拉丁语 pungere（刺）→ punctum（刺痕、点）→ 古法语 poinçon（尖锥）→ 英语 punch（打孔、出拳）；一为印地语 panch（五）→ 英语 punch（潘趣酒）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a sharp point driven in hard; the senses divide into the fist blow, the hole it makes, the tool that makes it, the force felt from it, and the unrelated five-part drink.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「一个尖点被重重压进去」；义项由此分为挥拳、打出的孔、打孔的工具、感受到的冲击力，以及与它们无关的五料饮品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed fist driven forward from the shoulder, landing on a sandbag that dents and swings back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只握紧的拳头从肩后送出，打在沙袋上，袋面凹下又荡回来。

branches.en: a fist landing on canvas
branches.cn: 落在帆布上的拳头

branches.en: a neat round hole in a ticket
branches.cn: 票面上一个整齐的圆孔

branches.en: a heavy press biting into steel plate
branches.cn: 压在钢板上的沉重冲床

branches.en: a last line that silences a room
branches.cn: 让全场安静下来的最后一句

branches.en: a wide bowl of red drink and floating fruit
branches.cn: 一大碗漂着果块的红酒饮

intro.en: The main line is held together by the Latin verb for pricking, its noun for a point, the French tool name, and the English endings built on them; the drink sits outside this family entirely.
intro.cn: 主线由表示刺的拉丁动词、指「点」的拉丁名词、法语工具名，以及由它们构成的英语后缀共同支撑；表示饮品的那条完全在这个词族之外。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

exactly on the point of time
