definition_zh: 炊具；炉灶；适合烹煮的水果
definition_en: a device or pot used for cooking, or a fruit that is good for cooking
core_image: 厨房角落一台白色炉灶，四个灶眼像四只安静的圆眼
scene: 搬进新家那天，母亲第一件事是擦净厨房里的炉灶。 She cleaned the cooker before unpacking the plates.
sceneCN: 这里 cooker 指「炉灶；炊具」（第 1 个义项：用来烹煮食物的器具）；句意是她先擦净炉灶，再拆开盘子。

collocations.phrase: put the pot on the cooker

senses.title: A device for cooking
senses.definition: a machine or large pot that is used to cook food
senses.definitionCN: 用来烹煮食物的机器或大锅
senses.example: The cooker has four rings and a small oven.
senses.exampleCN: 这台炉灶有四个灶眼和一个小烤箱。
senses.why: The tool takes the name of the act it exists to serve.
senses.whyCN: 工具借用了它生来要服务的那个动作的名字。

senses.title: A fruit for cooking
senses.definition: a fruit, especially an apple, grown to be cooked rather than eaten raw
senses.definitionCN: 专门用于烹煮而非生吃的水果，尤指苹果
senses.example: These cookers are too sour to eat raw.
senses.exampleCN: 这些煮食苹果太酸，不能生吃。
senses.why: Some fruit is grown for the pot, not for the hand.
senses.whyCN: 有些水果是为锅种的，不是为手种的。

intro.en: Cooker is cook plus the agent ending -er, which first named a person and later the machine.
intro.cn: cooker 是 cook 加施事词尾 -er，最初指人，后来指机器。

items.en: Coc named the person who prepared food.
items.cn: coc 指准备食物的人。

items.en: The verb coken described the work done at the fire.
items.cn: 动词 coken 描述在火边干的活。

items.en: Cooker first meant a person employed to cook.
items.cn: cooker 最初指受雇做饭的人。

items.en: With new kitchen machines, cooker shifted to the device itself.
items.cn: 随着厨房机器出现，cooker 转指器具本身。

items.en: Compounds like rice cooker and slow cooker are now common.
items.cn: rice cooker 与 slow cooker 之类的复合词如今很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short cook- base, and the meaning group names other kitchen words for heat and cooking.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 cook- 词基，近义组列出其他与加热和烹煮有关的厨房词。

entries.definition: to prepare food with heat
the skill of preparing food
a small sweet biscuit
a device with burners for cooking
a closed box for baking food
entries.definitionCN: 用来烘烤食物的封闭箱体

entries.definition: a large cooker with an oven

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a stove in a new kitchen, then move to fruit grown for the pot.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从新厨房里的一台炉灶开始，再到为锅而种的水果。

normal.en: Cook plus -er makes the thing that cooks, just as print plus -er makes the printer.
normal.cn: cook 加 -er 就是会煮东西的物件，正如 print 加 -er 是打印机。

normal.en: A cook is a person; a cooker is a machine.
normal.cn: cook 是人，cooker 是机器。

normal.en: In British homes the cooker is the whole stove, not just one pot.
normal.cn: 在英国家里，cooker 指整台炉灶，而不只是一口锅。

normal.en: Rice cooker and slow cooker show the word at work in compounds.
normal.cn: rice cooker 与 slow cooker 展示了这个词在复合词中的用法。

normal.en: A cooker apple is named for what will happen to it, not for how it tastes raw.
normal.cn: 煮食苹果是按它将要经历的事命名的，不是按生吃的味道。

abstract.en: Picture four round burners glowing in a dark kitchen.
abstract.cn: 想象暗厨房里四个圆形灶眼发着光。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy lid rattling on a pot.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的锅盖在锅上轻轻震动。

abstract.en: Picture a basket of sour apples beside a saucepan.
abstract.cn: 想象一篮酸苹果放在深锅旁边。

examples.en: She wiped the cooker after every meal.
examples.cn: 她每顿饭后都擦一遍炉灶。

examples.en: A rice cooker saves time on busy evenings.
examples.cn: 忙碌的晚上，电饭锅能省下时间。

examples.en: The old cooker gave off a smell of gas.
examples.cn: 那台旧炉灶散发出煤气味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cooker 记成 cook（煮）加 er（东西）：用来煮东西的物件，就是炉灶与炊具。

root: 由 cook（烹饪）加施事词尾 -er 构成，本指做饭的人，十九世纪起转指炉灶等炊事器具。

sensesIntro.en: From the person who cooks, to the machine that does the work, and to fruit meant for the pot.
sensesIntro.cn: 从做饭的人，到承担这项工作的机器，再到为锅而种的水果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white stove with four quiet burners.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台有四个安静灶眼的白色炉灶。

branches.en: A machine holds the heat that cooks the meal.
branches.cn: 机器承住热量，把饭煮熟。

branches.en: A fruit is chosen for the pot rather than the plate.
branches.cn: 一种水果被选中进锅，而不是上盘生吃。

branches.en: Both senses tie an object to the act of cooking.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把某样东西系在烹煮这个动作上。

branches.en: The device sense grew from the older word for a person.
branches.cn: 器具义项是从更早指人的词义长出来的。

branches.en: The fruit sense is local and survives mainly in British speech.
branches.cn: 水果义项较地方化，主要保留在英式说法里。

intro.en: Cooker is cook plus -er, the old ending for a person or thing that does an action.
intro.cn: cooker 是 cook 加 -er，这个古老词尾表示做某动作的人或物。

latinIntro.en: The cooking base coqu- also shows in cuisine, concoct and biscuit.
latinIntro.cn: 烹饪词基 coqu- 也出现在 cuisine、concoct 与 biscuit 中。

definition_zh: 出席；在场；存在；风度；气场
definition_en: the state of being in a place or of existing, and the impression a person makes by being there
core_image: 空椅子旁忽然多了一个人，屋里的人不自觉地把目光移过去
scene: 会议室里人到齐了，主位还空着，门一响，那位迟到的顾问走进来，屋里立刻安静。 Her presence at the meeting made everyone sit up straight.
sceneCN: 这里 presence 指「在场、出席」（第 1 个义项：人就在现场）；句意为她一出现在会上，所有人就坐直了。图中可辨识场景：长桌、空着的主位、刚进门的顾问。

derivatives.zh: 与 presence 同出拉丁语 praesens，义为「在场的；现在的」
由 present 加 -ly 构成，义为「不久；目前」
由 omni-（全部）与 presence 复合，义为「无所不在」

senses.title: The state of being in a particular place
senses.definition: the fact of being in a place and not absent
senses.definitionCN: 身处某地、没有缺席的事实
senses.example: Your presence at the ceremony would mean a lot to her.
senses.exampleCN: 你若出席典礼，对她意义重大。
senses.why: The Latin participle praesens means being before someone's eyes, so the first sense is simply the body being there.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语分词 praesens 意为「在某人眼前」，所以最基本的义项就是身体确实在那里，能被看见。

senses.title: The fact that something exists in a place
senses.definition: the fact that a substance, quality, or thing exists in a particular place or situation
senses.definitionCN: 某种物质、性质或事物存在于某处或某种情况之中
senses.example: Tests confirmed the presence of mercury in the water.
senses.exampleCN: 检测确认水中存在汞。
senses.why: If being before the eyes is the core, then anything that makes itself detectable is said to be present, even when it cannot be seen.
senses.whyCN: 既然核心是「出现在眼前」，那么任何能被察觉的东西都可以说成 present，即使肉眼看不见，细菌、汞也能「在场」。

senses.title: The impression made by a person's manner
senses.definition: the quality of a person's manner and bearing that makes others notice or respect them
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的举止与仪态给人留下印象、令人注意或敬重的气质
senses.example: The young actor has remarkable stage presence.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻演员有出众的舞台魅力。
senses.why: A person who fills a room simply by standing there seems to turn visible being into influence, which is why the word comes to mean bearing.
senses.whyCN: 一个人只站着就撑满整个房间，等于把「被看见的存在」变成一种影响力，于是这个词从「在场」长出了「气场」。

senses.title: A person or thing that is present but not seen
senses.definition: a person or thing that is in a place, especially one felt rather than seen, such as a spirit or a military force
senses.definitionCN: 身处某处的人或物，尤指只能感觉到而看不见的，如幽灵或军事力量
senses.example: She felt a strange presence in the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得空房子里有个奇怪的存在。
senses.why: Once the word can name any detectable thing, an unseen figure or a foreign army also counts as a presence, because what matters is the effect, not the visibility.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指任何可察觉之物，看不见的身影或驻扎的外国军队也能叫 presence，因为重点是它造成的影响，而不是能否看见。

intro.en: Presence comes from a Latin prefix meaning before joined to the verb to be; it names, quite literally, the state of being before someone.
intro.cn: presence 来自表示「在前」的拉丁前缀与动词「存在」的组合，字面上就是「在某人面前存在」的状态。

items.en: Prae- meant before or in front, the same prefix that marks what stands ahead of us.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，用来标示站在我们之前的东西。

items.en: Esse was the verb to be, the source of many forms in the Latin verb system and one of its oldest words.
items.cn: esse 是表示「存在、是」的动词，也是拉丁语动词系统中最古老的一组形式之一。

items.en: Praesens, the participle of praeesse, described what is before one, at hand, or in sight.
items.cn: praesens 是 praeesse 的分词，描述「在某人面前、在手边、在视野中」的东西。

items.en: The noun praesentia named the state of being there, and it passed into Old French as presence.
items.cn: 名词 praesentia 指「在场」的状态，进入古法语后写作 presence。

items.en: English uses presence for a body in a room, for anything that exists, and for the impression a person carries.
items.cn: 现代英语用 presence 指人在屋里、事物存在，以及一个人带来的气场。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin participle of being; the near-meaning group gathers words for attendance, existence and personal bearing.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「存在」的拉丁分词；近义组收出席、存在与个人气质方面的词。

entries.definition: Being in a place, or existing now.
Soon, or at the present time.
The state of being everywhere at once.
Knowledge of events before they happen; the word comes from another root meaning to know, so it is only similar in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 预知未来的能力；此词来自另一表示「知道」的词根，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The act of being present at an event.
The state of being real or alive.
entries.definitionCN: 真实存在或生存的状态。

entries.definition: A quality that seems to surround a person.
entries.definitionCN: 似乎环绕在人身周的气质。

entries.definition: The way a person stands and moves.

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin verb to be with a prefix meaning before, and its family keeps measuring how close something is to the room.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是表示「存在」的拉丁动词加表示「在前」的前缀，同族词都在衡量某物离这个房间有多近。

normal.en: Pre- plus esse: presence is literally being before someone, which is why the word starts with the body in the room.
normal.cn: pre- 加 esse：presence 字面就是「在某人面前存在」，所以起点是身体在屋里。

normal.en: Absent is the same verb with ab-, away: away from being, therefore not in the room.
normal.cn: absent 是同一个动词加 ab-（离开）：离开存在，因此不在屋里。

normal.en: The adjective present and the noun presence share one Latin participle, which is why both point to being here.
normal.cn: 形容词 present 与名词 presence 共用一个拉丁分词，所以都指向「在这里」。

normal.en: Presently can mean soon because what is at hand is about to arrive.
normal.cn: presently 能表示「不久」，因为在手边的东西马上就要到了。

normal.en: Omnipresence joins omni-, all, to presence: being everywhere at once.
normal.cn: omnipresence 把表示「全部」的 omni- 与 presence 结合，就是同时无所不在。

abstract.en: A room feels different the moment one person walks in, and that change is exactly what the word names.
abstract.cn: 一个人走进来的瞬间，屋里的感觉就变了，这个词命名的正是这种变化。

abstract.en: Presence is being seen without speaking: no words, only the fact of occupying space.
abstract.cn: presence 是不说话也被看见：没有言语，只有占据空间这件事。

abstract.en: The same root gives absent and present, so the word measures distance from the room.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根给出 absent 与 present，这个词量的其实是离房间的距离。

examples.en: Her presence at the meeting made everyone sit up straight.
examples.cn: 她一出现在会上，所有人就坐直了。

examples.en: The doctor noted the presence of a slight fever.
examples.cn: 医生注意到有轻微发热。

examples.en: The old house seemed to hold a presence of its own.
examples.cn: 这座老房子似乎自有一种存在感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音近「普瑞森斯」——贵人一到场，森森的安静就跟着来，presence 就是那种在场感。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ esse（存在）→ praesens（在眼前的）→ praesentia（在场），经古法语 presence 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being before someone's eyes; the senses run from a body in the room to anything that exists, then to the impression a person leaves.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「出现在某人眼前」；义项从人在屋里，扩展到任何事物的存在，再到一个人留下的气场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one more figure standing in a room that was already full.
core.cn: 核心意象：原本坐满的房间里，多出一个站着的人。

branches.en: a chair pulled out for the late guest
branches.cn: 为迟到的客人拉开一把椅子

branches.en: a test strip changing colour in a glass of water
branches.cn: 试纸在一杯水里变色

branches.en: a silent actor who owns the stage without a line
branches.cn: 不发一言却撑住舞台的演员

branches.en: a cold spot in a house nobody wants to enter
branches.cn: 无人敢进的屋子里那块冷处

branches.en: a quiet arrival that changes the mood of the room
branches.cn: 一次安静的到场改变了屋里的气氛

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin verb to be, its participle, and two English endings that turn the state into a noun and related adjectives.
intro.cn: 这个词依托拉丁语动词「存在」、它的分词，以及把状态变成名词和相关形容词的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: not here, formed with ab- away

definition_zh: 证据；证明；校样；检验；防…的；能抵挡…的
definition_en: facts or evidence showing that something is true, a trial copy of printed work, or, as an adjective, able to resist something
core_image: 一样东西被反复检验过，最后摆到桌上当作凭据
scene: 实验室的桌上摊着一叠材料，研究员把每一次测量都抄进本子，好让结论站得住脚。 The team needed proof that the new filter actually removed the salt.
sceneCN: 这里取「证据」的意思（第 1 个义项：能证明某事为真的材料）；句意为团队需要证据，证明新滤芯确实去掉了盐分。桌上那叠记录就是他们正在攒的东西。

derivatives.zh: 与 proof 同出拉丁词干 probare，义为「证明；证实」
由 proof 与 read 复合而成，义为「校对」
由 water 与 proof 复合而成，义为「防水的」
由拉丁词干 prob- 加 -able 构成，义为「很可能的」

senses.title: Evidence that something is true
senses.definition: facts, information or objects that show that something is true or really exists
senses.definitionCN: 能表明某事为真或确实存在的事实、信息或物件
senses.example: The police found no proof that he had been there.
senses.exampleCN: 警方没有找到他当时在场的证据。
senses.why: Latin probare meant to test and to judge as good, so a proof is literally what comes out of a test: the word names the result before it names the argument.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 probare 意为检验并判断好坏，所以 proof 字面上就是检验之后出来的东西：它先指结果，然后才指论证。

senses.title: A logical or mathematical demonstration
senses.definition: a series of steps showing that a statement must be true, especially in mathematics or logic
senses.definitionCN: 尤其用于数学或逻辑，用一串步骤表明某个命题必然成立
senses.example: The proof took three pages and ended with a single line.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明写了三页，最后只归结为一行。
senses.why: If a proof is what a test yields, then a chain of reasoning is the strictest test available: every step checks the one before it and leaves no room for doubt.
senses.whyCN: 既然 proof 是检验的产物，那么一串推理就是最严格的检验：每一步都在核对前一步，不留怀疑的余地。

senses.title: A trial print checked for errors
senses.definition: a copy of printed or photographed work made before the final version so that mistakes can still be corrected
senses.definitionCN: 在定稿之前印出的一份副本，以便还能改正错误
senses.example: She read the proof of her article and marked two typos.
senses.exampleCN: 她读了文章的校样，标出两处排印错误。
senses.why: Printers once pulled a sheet off the press to test the type, and the sheet used for that test simply inherited the name of the test itself.
senses.whyCN: 从前印刷工要从机器上抽一张纸来验版，用来验版的那张纸就直接继承了「检验」这个名字。

senses.title: Able to resist something
senses.definition: strong enough to keep something out or to resist damage, used after a noun or with against
senses.definitionCN: 足以把某物挡在外面或不受损伤，常后置或与 against 连用
senses.example: The jacket is proof against wind and rain.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套防风又防雨。
senses.why: Something that has been tested and has not failed is trusted, so proof turned into an adjective for materials that have already survived the test of wind, water or fire.
senses.whyCN: 经得住检验、没有失手的东西才可信，于是 proof 转成形容词，指已经扛过风、水或火考验的材料。

senses.title: A test of quality
senses.definition: an act of testing whether something is good enough, or the standard it has to reach
senses.definitionCN: 检验某物是否够好的动作，或它必须达到的标准
senses.example: The pudding is the proof of the cook.
senses.exampleCN: 布丁好坏，一尝便知厨师本事。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the word kept almost untouched: proof as the trial itself, before it came to mean the evidence that the trial produced.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层，几乎原样留着：proof 指检验这件事本身，早于它指检验得出的证据。

intro.en: Proof descends from a Latin verb meaning to test, and that testing sense still explains both the evidence and the printed sheet.
intro.cn: proof 出自一个意为「检验」的拉丁动词，正是这层「检验」的意思同时解释了「证据」与「校样」。

items.en: Probare meant to test, to examine and to judge as good, and the adjective probus described something upright and sound.
items.cn: probare 意为检验、查验、判定为好，形容词 probus 指正直、可靠的。

items.en: A noun proba grew from the verb and named a trial or a test of something's quality.
items.cn: 由动词产生名词 proba，指试验、对某物品质的检验。

items.en: Old French carried the noun on as prueve or proeve, still meaning a trial and the evidence it produced.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 prueve 或 proeve，仍指试验以及试验得出的凭据。

items.en: Middle English borrowed two forms of the same French word, and they settled into different jobs: proof for the noun, prove for the verb.
items.cn: 中古英语从同一个法语词借入两种形式，随后分工固定下来：proof 作名词，prove 作动词。

items.en: Modern English extends proof to printed proofs, mathematical proofs and, as an adjective, to materials that resist water, wind or bullets.
items.cn: 现代英语把 proof 扩展到印刷校样、数学证明，以及作形容词时指防水、防风、防弹的材料。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin stem of testing; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for what supports a claim.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「检验」词干上的词；近义组收支撑某个说法的名词。

entries.definition: To show that something is true.
Likely to be true or to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能是真的或会发生的。

entries.definition: A period of testing a person's behaviour or ability.
entries.definitionCN: 考查某人表现或能力的试用期。

entries.definition: To accept something as good enough.
Facts that support a belief or a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 支持某种看法或说法的事实。

entries.definition: A clear showing that something is true.
The act of checking that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事是否属实的动作。

entries.definition: A formal statement, especially in court.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指法庭上的正式陈述。

normalIntro.en: The word is a thing held up after testing, and its family keeps returning to trials, checks and the trust that follows them.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一件检验之后被举起示人的东西，同族词反复回到试验、查验以及随之而来的信任。

normal.en: Latin probare means to test, so proof and prove are two branches of one testing root, not two unrelated words.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 probare 意为检验，所以 proof 与 prove 是同一「检验」词根的两支，并非两个无关的词。

normal.en: The noun proof and the verb prove came from two forms of the same French word, which is why they differ by a single letter.
normal.cn: 名词 proof 与动词 prove 来自同一个法语词的两种形式，所以两者只差一个字母。

normal.en: Probable, probation and approve all grow from the same stem: something judged likely, a testing period, and a test passed.
normal.cn: probable、probation、approve 都长在同一词干上：被判为可能、一段考查期，以及通过了考查。

normal.en: A printing proof is the sheet pulled to test the type, so the word can name the test and the thing tested at the same time.
normal.cn: 印刷校样是为验版抽出的那张纸，所以这个词能同时指检验和被检验的东西。

normal.en: Proof as an adjective grew from proof against something: a coat proof against rain has survived the test of rain.
normal.cn: 作形容词的 proof 从 proof against 长出来：proof against rain 的外套，就是扛住了雨的考验。

abstract.en: A proof is not the truth itself but the trace a test leaves, which is why evidence and demonstration can share the word.
abstract.cn: 证据不是真理本身，而是检验留下的痕迹，所以「证据」与「论证」能共用一个词。

abstract.en: To be proof against something is a promise about the future made on the strength of a test in the past.
abstract.cn: 说某物防得住，是凭过去的检验对未来作出的承诺。

abstract.en: Every proof is addressed to someone who doubts, so the word always carries a listener inside it.
abstract.cn: 每一份证据都是说给怀疑者听的，所以这个词里始终藏着一个听众。

examples.en: The police found no proof that he had been there.
examples.cn: 警方没有找到他当时在场的证据。

examples.en: This jacket is proof against wind and rain.
examples.cn: 这件外套防风又防雨。

examples.en: She read the proof of her article and marked two typos.
examples.cn: 她读了文章的校样，标出两处排印错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑如夫」——像「扑上去验」，扑过去仔细查一遍，验出来的就是证据。

root: 拉丁语 probare（检验、验明）产生晚期拉丁语名词 proba（检验），经古法语 prueve 进入英语；名词写作 proof，动词写作 prove，本是一个词分出的两支。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a test and what it yields; the senses divide into the evidence produced, the reasoning that serves as the strictest test, the sheet tested at the press, the material that passed a test, and the test itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「检验及其结果」；义项分成检验得出的证据、最严格的一种检验即推理、印刷时被验的那张纸、通过考验的材料，以及检验这件事本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object that has been put through a test and is now held up on the table as the record of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件经过检验的东西被举到桌上，当作检验的记录。

branches.en: a folder of documents laid on a table
branches.cn: 摊在桌上的一叠文件

branches.en: a blackboard filled with numbered steps
branches.cn: 写满编号步骤的黑板

branches.en: a printed sheet with red marks in the margin
branches.cn: 页边画着红笔的校样

branches.en: a coat with rain running off it
branches.cn: 雨水顺着外套流下

branches.en: a spoon lifted from a pudding
branches.cn: 从布丁里舀起的一勺

intro.en: A Latin verb of testing and the noun it produced hold the word together; English then split the noun and the verb into two spellings.
intro.cn: 表示检验的拉丁语动词及由其产生的名词共同支撑这个词；英语随后把名词与动词分成两种拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin probare, to test, its adjective probus, sound, and the Late Latin noun proba, a trial, stand behind the English noun and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 probare（检验）、形容词 probus（可靠的）与晚期拉丁语名词 proba（检验）是英语名词与动词背后的来源。

definition_zh: 不断地；一再地；始终
definition_en: in a way that keeps happening without a real break
core_image: 秒针一圈圈走过，从不停下
scene: 她一边打电话，一边在门口来回走动。 He is constantly checking whether the door is locked.
sceneCN: 这里 constantly 指「不断地」（第 1 个义项：反复而不停歇）；句意是他不停地确认门有没有锁好。

senses.title: Without stopping
senses.definition: continuing without any real break
senses.definitionCN: 持续进行而几乎没有间断
senses.example: The machine runs constantly all night.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器整夜不停地运转。
senses.why: Some processes only stop when the power does.
senses.whyCN: 有些过程只在断电时才停下。

senses.title: Again and again
senses.definition: repeating so often that it starts to annoy
senses.definitionCN: 重复得太多，已经开始惹人烦
senses.example: He constantly interrupts me.
senses.exampleCN: 他一再打断我。
senses.why: A habit repeated too often turns into noise.
senses.whyCN: 重复太多的习惯，会变成噪音。

senses.title: All the while
senses.definition: during the whole of a period, without a gap
senses.definitionCN: 在整个一段时间里，没有间断
senses.example: She was constantly aware of the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 她始终留意着那只钟。
senses.why: A quiet state can last as long as the day does.
senses.whyCN: 一种安静的状态，可以和一天一样长。

intro.en: Constantly is constant plus -ly, from Latin constans, standing firm, which comes from constare, to stand together.
intro.cn: constantly 是 constant 加 -ly，源自拉丁语 constans（稳稳站住），其词根是 constare（一起站立）。

items.en: Stare meant to stand, and constare meant to stand firm.
items.cn: stare 意为站立，constare 意为站稳。

items.en: Constans described what kept its place and nature.
items.cn: constans 描述守住位置与本性的事物。

items.en: French constant passed the steady sense into English.
items.cn: 法语 constant 把稳定的含义带进英语。

items.en: The adverb constantli first meant in a steady manner.
items.cn: 副词形式最初指以稳定的方式。

items.en: It widened to mean again and again over time.
items.cn: 它的词义扩大为在时间中反复发生。

items.en: Today it often carries a hint of complaint.
items.cn: 今天它常带一点抱怨的意味。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the constant- family or the -antly ending, and the meaning group names other words for repeated action.
note.cn: 形近组共享 constant- 词族或 -antly 词尾，近义组列出其他表示反复动作的词。

entries.definition: happening all the time without a pause
the quality of staying the same
at once, with no delay at all
repeatedly over a period of time
many times, one after another
at every time, on every occasion

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a second hand that never rests, then move to an annoying habit and to a state that lasts all day.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从不休息的秒针开始，再到惹人烦的习惯，最后到持续一整天的状态。

normal.en: Constant plus -ly turns a standing thing into an action that never sits down.
normal.cn: constant 加上 -ly，把站住的东西变成一个从不停下的动作。

normal.en: A dripping tap is the sound of constantly.
normal.cn: 滴水的水龙头就是 constantly 的声音。

normal.en: If a friend says it three times before lunch, it is happening constantly.
normal.cn: 若朋友在午饭前说了三遍，那就是一再地发生。

normal.en: Constant is the state, constantly is the motion.
normal.cn: constant 是状态，constantly 是动作。

normal.en: The clock does not decide to be regular; it just is.
normal.cn: 钟并不决定要规律，它本来就这样。

abstract.en: Picture a second hand sweeping the same circle.
abstract.cn: 想象一根秒针扫过同一个圆圈。

abstract.en: Picture small waves hitting the same stone.
abstract.cn: 想象细小的浪一遍遍拍打同一块石头。

abstract.en: Picture a light left on above a shop door.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店门上方一直亮着的灯。

examples.en: She constantly checks her messages during dinner.
examples.cn: 吃饭时她不停地看消息。

examples.en: The two brothers are constantly arguing.
examples.cn: 这两兄弟老是争吵。

examples.en: Prices have been constantly rising this year.
examples.cn: 今年物价一直在上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 constantly 记成 constant（恒定的）加 ly：以恒定不变的方式一遍遍发生，就是不断地。

root: 由 constant 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，constant 源自拉丁语 constare（com 一起 + stare 站立），本义是稳稳站住，故 constantly 指不间断地、一再地。

sensesIntro.en: From a process with no pause, to a habit that repeats too often, and to a state that lasts all day.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有停顿的过程，到重复过多的习惯，最后到持续一整天的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clock hand that never stops moving.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根从不停下的钟表指针。

branches.en: The first sense is motion with no gap at all.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是毫无间隙的运动。

branches.en: The second sense is repetition frequent enough to irritate.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是频繁到令人烦躁的重复。

branches.en: The third sense is a state held across a whole period.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是贯穿整段时间的状态。

branches.en: Both senses describe something that fills time without a hole.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述填满时间、没有空洞的事物。

branches.en: What happens all the while is often what we later call a habit.
branches.cn: 始终在发生的事，后来常被我们叫作习惯。

intro.en: Constantly is built from the Latin base stant-, standing, plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: constantly 由拉丁语词基 stant-（站立）加副词词尾 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stand base also appears in constant, constancy and stable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的站立词基也出现在 constant、constancy 与 stable 中。

items.meaning: in a way that never really stops

items.exampleCN: 他的忠贞赢得了她的信任。

items.example: An inconstant wind filled the sails.
items.exampleCN: 一阵忽强忽弱的风鼓起了帆。

items.meaning: the way a body or a mind stands
items.example: He took a firm stance on the issue.
items.exampleCN: 他在这个问题上立场坚定。

items.meaning: to hold firmly to a demand
items.example: He insisted on a second chance.

definition_zh: 目击者；证人；证词；目击；见证（某事件）
definition_en: a person who sees an event happen, and to see or to give evidence about an event
core_image: 街角的一个路人停下脚步，眼睛一直没离开那扇正在被推开的门
scene: 事故发生时，街角有个路人停下脚步，一直盯着那扇被撞开的门。 The only witness to the accident was a boy of twelve.
sceneCN: 这里 witness 是「目击者」（第 1 个义项：亲眼看见某事发生的人）；句意为事故唯一的目击者是一个十二岁的男孩。街角那个停下脚步、眼睛不离开的人，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: A person who saw it
senses.definition: a person who was present and saw an event with their own eyes
senses.definitionCN: 在场并亲眼看见某事件的个人
senses.example: The only witness to the accident was a boy of twelve.
senses.exampleCN: 事故唯一的目击者是一个十二岁的男孩。
senses.why: The old noun came from a word meaning knowledge, so a witness was first simply someone who knew.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老名词来自意为「知识」的词，所以 witness 起初只是知道的人。

senses.title: A person in a court
senses.definition: someone who tells a court under oath what they saw or know
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上宣誓讲述所见所知的人
senses.example: She appeared as a witness for the family.
senses.exampleCN: 她作为这家人的证人出庭。
senses.why: The same knowledge is now official: the witness speaks to a judge and the words become evidence.
senses.whyCN: 同样的知识成了正式的：证人向法官陈说，其话成为证据。

senses.title: To see an event happen
senses.definition: used of a person, place or time that sees an event take place
senses.definitionCN: 用于人、地点或时代看见某事件发生
senses.example: That year witnessed the biggest flood in a century.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年发生了一世纪以来最大的洪水。
senses.why: Places and years can be said to witness, so the word widens from people to the settings of events.
senses.whyCN: 地点与年份也能「见证」，于是这个词从人扩展到事件的发生场景。

senses.title: To show that something is true
senses.definition: to provide evidence of a fact, in phrases such as bear witness to
senses.definitionCN: 在 bear witness to 等说法中，为某事实提供证明
senses.example: The empty shelves bore witness to the long drought.
senses.exampleCN: 空空的货架说明旱情已久。
senses.why: If a person can tell what happened, then an object can also stand as a silent proof of it.
senses.whyCN: 如果人能讲述发生了什么，物件也能成为它的无声证明。

intro.en: Witness comes from Old English witnes, formed from witan, to know, so the witness was the one who knows what happened.
intro.cn: witness 来自古英语 witnes，由 witan（知道）构成，所以证人就是知道发生了什么的人。

items.en: witnes meant knowledge as well as a person who has it, built on witan, to know.
items.cn: witnes 既指知识，也指拥有知识的人，建于 witan（知道）之上。

items.en: The word moved towards the legal sense, a person who reports what he saw.
items.cn: 这个词转向法律义，指报告自己所见的人。

items.en: To bear witness and to call a witness fixed the noun in legal speech.
items.cn: bear witness 与 call a witness 让名词在法律语言里固定下来。

items.en: The verb came to be used of places and periods that see great events.
items.cn: 动词开始用于看见大事的地点与时期。

items.en: Silent objects, from a broken wall to an empty shelf, can now bear witness as well.
items.cn: 无声的物件，从断墙到空货架，如今也能作证。

note.en: The first group gathers same-family and look-alike words, the second other names for someone who reports events.
note.cn: 第一组收同族与形近词，第二组收其他指讲述事件者的称呼。

normalIntro.en: Witness is wit plus -ness, so the spelling keeps a single t in the middle and a single n after it.
normalIntro.cn: witness 是 wit 加 -ness，所以中间只有一个 t，后面只有一个 n。

normal.en: Wit plus ness: the one who has wit and knows what happened.
normal.cn: wit 加 ness：有见识、知道发生了什么的那个人。

normal.en: Do not double the t: it is wit, not witt, before ness.
normal.cn: t 不要写两个：加 ness 前是 wit 而非 witt。

normal.en: The plural takes -es after the s sound of ness.
normal.cn: 复数在 ness 后的 s 音后加 -es。

normal.en: An eye witness is a witness with eyes, which is all a witness ever is.
normal.cn: eye witness 意为带眼睛的证人，而证人本来就是眼睛。

normal.en: Bear witness means carry the proof, as one bears a heavy thing to court.
normal.cn: bear witness 意为把证据扛到法庭，如扛起重物。

abstract.en: Feet stopping at a corner and not moving.
abstract.cn: 在街角停住、不再移动的脚步。

abstract.en: Eyes fixed on a door as it opens.
abstract.cn: 门被推开时那双不移的眼睛。

abstract.en: A hand raised in a silent room, ready to speak.
abstract.cn: 安静的房间里举起、准备开口的手。

examples.en: Two witnesses described the same car.
examples.cn: 两名目击者描述的是同一辆车。

examples.en: We are witnessing the end of an old habit.
examples.cn: 我们正在见证一种旧习惯的终结。

examples.en: The marks on the wall bear witness to the flood.
examples.cn: 墙上的痕迹证明了那次洪水。

dict_mnemonic.text: wit（知道）+ ness —— 知道真相的那个人，就是「证人」。

root: 古英语 witan（知道）→ witnes（知识；知情者）→ witness；同族有 eyewitness、wit。

sensesIntro.en: The one who knows becomes the one who speaks in court, then the verb spreads to places and years, and finally to silent objects.
sensesIntro.cn: 知道的人成为在法庭上讲述的人，接着动词扩展到地点与年份，最后扩到无声的物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a passer-by stopped dead at a corner, watching.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角一个停住脚步的路人在看。

chain: A PLACE OR YEAR THAT SEES

branches.en: The observer branch: a boy of twelve at the corner.
branches.cn: 观察者分支：街角上十二岁的男孩。

branches.en: The court branch: a family's supporter on the stand.
branches.cn: 法庭分支：证人席上支持那家人的她。

branches.en: The event branch: a year that saw a great flood.
branches.cn: 事件分支：见到大洪水的那一年。

branches.en: The proof branch: marks on a wall that tell the story.
branches.cn: 证据分支：墙上讲述往事的痕迹。

branches.en: The evidence branch: seeing and proving are the same act.
branches.cn: 证据分支：看见与证明是同一个行为。

intro.en: Witness is the stem wit with the noun ending -ness; the same history gives the adjective witnessly in old texts.
intro.cn: witness 是词干 wit 加名词词尾 -ness；同样来历在古文中还留下 witnessly 这样的形式。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin entry shows the borrowed legal word for a witness, still used in testis-based terms.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属于日耳曼语；拉丁条目给出法律上的借入词，仍留在以 testis 为词根的说法里。

items.exampleCN: 身份给了一处地方命名。

definition_zh: 调味汁；酱汁；沙司
definition_en: a thick liquid served with food to add flavour
core_image: 一勺浓稠的番茄酱浇在热气腾腾的意大利面上
scene: 厨房里，妈妈把酱汁浇在面条上。 Mom poured the sauce over the noodles.
sceneCN: 这里 sauce 是「调味汁」（第 1 个义项）；句意：妈妈把酱汁浇在了面条上。

senses.title: Flavoured liquid
senses.definition: a thick liquid served with food to add flavour
senses.definitionCN: 与食物一起食用、用来增添风味的浓稠液体
senses.example: She made a rich tomato sauce for the pasta.
senses.exampleCN: 她为意面做了一份浓郁的番茄酱。
senses.why: The basic sense is a liquid that flavours food.
senses.whyCN: 基本义是给食物增添风味的液体。

senses.title: Cooking juices
senses.definition: the juice that comes from meat while it is cooking
senses.definitionCN: 肉在烹制过程中流出的汁液
senses.example: The roast beef was served with its own sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 烤牛肉配着它自身的肉汁一起上桌。
senses.why: Natural cooking juices work like a sauce.
senses.whyCN: 烹制时流出的天然汁液起着酱汁的作用。

senses.title: Audacity
senses.definition: rude or cheeky behaviour, used informally
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用语，指无礼或冒失的行为
senses.example: Nobody has the sauce to argue with her.
senses.exampleCN: 没人敢冒失地跟她争辩。
senses.why: The flavour image shifts to a bold and sharp manner.
senses.whyCN: 从味道的形象引申为大胆而带刺的态度。

intro.en: Sauce comes from Latin salsus, meaning salted, through Old French.
intro.cn: sauce 源自拉丁语 salsus（盐腌的），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Salsus means salted, from sal, salt.
items.cn: salsus 意为盐腌的，来自 sal（盐）。

items.en: Salsa meant a salted or seasoned preparation.
items.cn: salsa 指盐腌或调味的食物。

items.en: Sauce named a seasoned liquid served with food.
items.cn: sauce 在古法语中指配食物的调味液体。

items.en: English borrowed sauce for liquid served with meat.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 sauce，指配肉食的液态调料。

items.en: Sauce now covers sweet, savoury, and figurative uses.
items.cn: 现代英语中 sauce 兼指甜酱、咸酱与引申义。

note.en: Sauce is compared with look-alike words and with other things served alongside food.
note.cn: 把 sauce 与形近词以及佐餐调料作比较。

entries.definition: a small shallow dish for a cup
a room filled with hot steam for bathing
to soak food in salty water
juice from cooked meat
a sauce poured over salad
a seasoning added to food

normalIntro.en: Sauce can be remembered by sound, image, and word family.
normalIntro.cn: 可以从读音、画面和词族三个角度记住 sauce。

normal.en: Think of sauce as the source of flavour on the plate.
normal.cn: 把 sauce 想成盘子里风味的来源，即 source。

normal.en: The round au in sauce looks like a drop of gravy.
normal.cn: sauce 中圆圆的 au 像一滴酱汁。

normal.en: Soy sauce and tomato sauce are two everyday examples.
normal.cn: 酱油和番茄酱是两个日常例子。

normal.en: Saucy means cheeky, just as sauce can mean audacity.
normal.cn: saucy 意为俏皮无礼，正如 sauce 可指冒失。

normal.en: The plural sauces simply adds s to the base word.
normal.cn: 复数 sauces 只需在词尾加 s。

abstract.en: Sauce is the seasoning that turns plain food into a treat.
abstract.cn: 酱汁是把普通食物变成美味的调味。

abstract.en: A little sauce can change the whole mood of a meal.
abstract.cn: 一点酱汁就能改变整顿饭的气氛。

abstract.en: Sauce hides neither the food nor itself; it blends both.
abstract.cn: 酱汁既不掩盖食物也不掩盖自己，而是让两者融合。

examples.en: The chef added a spoonful of sauce to the rice.
examples.cn: 厨师往米饭里加了一勺酱汁。

examples.en: Too much sauce can hide the taste of the fish.
examples.cn: 酱汁太多会盖住鱼的味道。

examples.en: She stirred the sauce slowly over low heat.
examples.cn: 她在小火上慢慢搅动酱汁。

dict_mnemonic.text: sauce 与 salt（盐）同源，最初指盐腌调味的液体，可记「一勺带咸香的酱汁」。

root: 源自拉丁语 salsus（盐腌的），经古法语 sauce 进入英语，核心义「加盐调味、配食物食用的液体」。

sensesIntro.en: Sauce means a flavoured liquid for food, natural cooking juices, or informally audacity.
sensesIntro.cn: sauce 意为给食物调味的液体、天然肉汁，或口语中的冒失无礼。

core.en: A seasoned liquid that adds flavour to food.
core.cn: 给食物增添风味的调味液体。

branches.en: The core sense, a flavoured liquid served with a dish.
branches.cn: 核心义，配菜食用的调味液体。

branches.en: Natural meat juices used as a sauce.
branches.cn: 用作酱汁的天然肉汁。

branches.en: Boldness, from spicy flavour to a sharp manner.
branches.cn: 由辛辣味道引申出的冒失态度。

branches.en: Everyday cooking links poured sauce and natural juices.
branches.cn: 日常烹饪把浇上的酱汁和天然肉汁联系起来。

branches.en: Rich juice and bold manner both suggest strength.
branches.cn: 浓郁的肉汁与大胆的态度都暗示强烈。

intro.en: Sauce belongs to a family of cooking and manner words.
intro.cn: sauce 属于一个兼指烹饪与态度的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin salsus, salted, is the distant source of sauce.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 salsus（盐腌的）是 sauce 的远源。
